title: RES 1B Chapter 2
answer_source: ticked options in the CMFAS Academy app, cross-checked against each question's explanation

questions.q: In relation to a CMS licence holder, what does the term assets of the customer include?
o: Government Securities.
Certificate of deposits.
Money.
Personal assets of the customer.
questions.e: "Customer's assets", in relation to the CMS licence holder, means securities and assets , including Government securities and certificates of deposits, that are beneficially owned by a customer of the CMS licence holder, but does not include moneys, and securities and assets received from or on account of a customer who is an institutional investor in connection with any OTC derivatives contract entered into by the CMS licence holder with the customer, is not cleared or settled by a clearing facility and is booked in Singapore.

questions.q:
Sophia, a provisional representative at Elite Advisors Ltd. ('Elite'), has been diligently working under the supervision of a senior advisor, John, to gain the necessary experience in advising clients on investment products. Sophia recently completed a certification that enhances her understanding of complex investment strategies. Eager to apply her new knowledge, she independently conducted a seminar for potential clients without informing John or obtaining approval from Elite. During the seminar, Sophia provided detailed investment advice to attendees.

According to the guidelines for provisional representatives, which of the following mistakes did Sophia make?
o: Conducting regulated activities without the necessary supervision and approval from her principal company.
Failing to update her qualifications in the Public Register of Representatives.
Not completing the minimum required period under provisional status before conducting seminars.
Engaging in promotional activities without the proper authorization and oversight.
questions.e: (A) and (C) are correct because provisional representatives must conduct their activities under supervision and cannot independently conduct seminars or provide advice without approval. (B) is incorrect because the scenario does not mention the need to update the Public Register of Representatives with her new certification. (D) is incorrect because it's not specified that promotional activities require separate authorization, but the lack of supervision and approval for her actions is the main issue.

questions.q:
At Summit Financial Group ('Summit'), a routine audit revealed that some client funds received for OTC derivatives contracts were not being deposited into a trust account as mandated. Additionally, it was found that funds received from institutional investors for OTC derivatives contracts were being commingled with Summit's operational funds.

According to the guidelines for moneys received on account of a customer, which of the following actions should Summit take to ensure compliance?
o: Deposit all moneys received on account of retail customers for OTC derivatives contracts into a trust account.
Deposit moneys received from institutional investors for OTC derivatives contracts into Summit's operational funds if consented by the investors.
Ensure that moneys received from any customer, including institutional investors, for OTC derivatives contracts are not commingled with Summit's operational funds.
Deposit moneys received from retail customers for any purpose other than OTC derivatives contracts into a separate operational account designated for client funds.
questions.e: (A) and (C) are correct because the guidelines mandate that all moneys received on account of retail customers for OTC derivatives contracts must be deposited into a trust account and that moneys received from any customer for OTC derivatives contracts should not be commingled with the firm's operational funds. (B) is incorrect because moneys received from institutional investors for OTC derivatives contracts should also be handled according to the guidelines, which do not allow commingling with operational funds without proper segregation. (D) is incorrect because it does not accurately reflect the guidelines' requirements for handling client funds.

questions.q:
Alex, a representative at Future Growth Investments ('Future Growth'), has been focusing on expanding his knowledge in the field of sustainable investments. Over the past year, he attended several workshops and online courses related to green finance and sustainable investment practices. However, Alex has not documented any of these activities nor informed Future Growth about his participation in these educational programs.

What should Alex have done differently according to the guidelines for continuing education for representatives?
o: Documented his participation in the workshops and online courses and informed Future Growth to ensure compliance with Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requirements.
Only focused on internal training programs provided by Future Growth as external courses do not count towards CPD.
Assumed that his self-study in sustainable investments would automatically be recognized by Future Growth without formal documentation.
Waited for Future Growth to assign him relevant training programs instead of seeking out his own educational opportunities.
questions.e: (A) is correct because representatives are expected to document their CPD activities and inform their principal companies to ensure these activities are recognized towards their CPD requirements. (B) is incorrect because external courses can count towards CPD if they are relevant to the representative's role and responsibilities. (C) is incorrect because formal documentation and notification are necessary for CPD activities to be recognized. (D) is incorrect because representatives are encouraged to proactively seek educational opportunities that align with their professional development needs.

questions.q:
Marcus, a newly appointed temporary representative at Quantum Financial Services ('Quantum'), is excited to start his role and is keen on making a strong impression. He has been working closely with clients on their investment portfolios, leveraging his previous experience in the financial sector. However, Marcus recently moved to a new apartment and forgot to inform Quantum of his change of address. Two weeks have passed since the move, and Marcus has not yet updated his personal particulars with Quantum.

What action should Marcus have taken according to the guidelines for representatives?
o: Inform Quantum of his change in personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change.
Wait for Quantum to request the update of his personal particulars during their annual review.
Assume that the change of address is not significant enough to report to Quantum.
Rely on Quantum's HR department to automatically update his address based on public records.
questions.e: (A) is correct because representatives are required to inform their principal company of any change in their identification or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change. (B), (C), and (D) are incorrect as they do not align with the guidelines that mandate proactive communication of any changes in personal particulars by the representative.

questions.q:
Jasmine, a provisional representative at Capital Wise Ltd. ('Capital Wise'), is keen on advancing her career and meeting the competency requirements for her role. She understands the importance of continuing education and wants to ensure she meets the MAS guidelines for CPD. Jasmine decides to enroll in a series of online courses covering regulatory compliance, ethics in finance, and advanced portfolio management. She plans to complete these courses over the next six months.

According to the guidelines for continuing education, which of the following actions should Jasmine take to comply with the CPD requirements?
o: Ensure the courses cover topics relevant to her role at Capital Wise and document her participation and completion of these courses.
Focus solely on courses offered by Capital Wise, as external courses are not recognized for CPD purposes.
Complete the courses but wait for an annual review with Capital Wise to discuss and document her CPD activities.
Assume that her participation in these courses will automatically be updated in the Public Register of Representatives without any action on her part.
questions.e: (A) is correct because representatives must ensure their CPD activities are relevant to their role and responsibilities, and they must document their participation and completion of these activities. (B) is incorrect because external courses can be recognized for CPD purposes if they are relevant and properly documented. (C) is incorrect because representatives should not wait for an annual review to document CPD activities; they should do so promptly upon completion. (D) is incorrect because representatives are responsible for informing their principal companies of their CPD activities; updates to the Public Register of Representatives require action by the principal company.

questions.q:
James, a portfolio manager at International Wealth Corp ('IWC'), is advising his client, Karen, on diversifying her investment portfolio by including overseas-listed investment products. Karen is new to investing in foreign markets and is unaware of the potential risks.

What is James required to do according to the guidelines for CMS licence holders dealing in overseas-listed investment products before Karen can proceed with her investment?
o: James should ensure Karen is aware of the key risks associated with overseas-listed investment products by providing her with a risk warning statement and obtaining her acknowledgement of understanding these risks before proceeding.
James should advise Karen to focus on local markets only, as investing in overseas markets requires advanced knowledge.
James should proceed with the investment if Karen insists, as client preference takes precedence over regulatory guidelines.
James should only provide Karen with a general disclaimer about the risks of investing in financial markets.
questions.e: (A) is correct because the guidelines require CMS licence holders to warn retail customers of the possible risks associated with overseas-listed investment products by providing a risk warning statement and obtaining the customer's acknowledgement before allowing transactions. (B), (C), and (D) are incorrect as they do not comply with the specific requirement to provide and obtain acknowledgement of a risk warning statement for overseas-listed investment products.

questions.q:
Laura, a financial advisor at Cross-Border Investments ('CBI'), is preparing to offer her clients a selection of overseas-listed investment products. She understands the importance of complying with regulatory requirements when dealing with such products.

According to the guidelines, what must Laura do to ensure compliance when offering overseas-listed investment products to her clients?
o: Laura must classify all overseas-listed investment products as Excluded Investment Products (EIPs) to simplify the compliance process.

Laura must provide a risk warning statement to her clients, highlighting the key risks of trading overseas-listed investment products, and obtain their written acknowledgement before their first trade.
Laura should assume that her clients are aware of the risks associated with overseas markets and proceed with offering the products without additional disclosures.
Laura must ensure that all overseas-listed investment products are pre-approved by regulatory authorities before offering them to her clients.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because not all overseas-listed investment products can be classified as EIPs without proper assessment. (B) is correct because CMS licence holders are required to provide clients with a risk warning statement that highlights the key risks associated with overseas-listed investment products and obtain their written acknowledgement before allowing the first trade. (C) is incorrect as assuming client awareness does not fulfill the requirement for providing a risk warning statement. (D) is incorrect because the requirement focuses on providing risk disclosures to clients, not on pre-approval of products by regulatory authorities.

questions.q:
Elena, a financial advisor at Zenith Wealth Management ('Zenith' - an exempt financial advisor), is assisting a new client, Tom, who is interested in trading unlisted Specified Investment Products (SIPs). Tom has a background in real estate investment but is new to the capital markets. Elena conducts a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) and finds that Tom lacks experience in SIPs. Despite this, Tom insists on proceeding with trading unlisted SIPs.

What should Elena do next according to the guidelines for Customer Account Review and Customer Knowledge Assessment?
o: Proceed with opening a SIP trading account for Tom since he insists on trading unlisted SIPs.
Advise Tom against trading unlisted SIPs until he gains the necessary knowledge or experience.
Open a SIP trading account for Tom but limit his trading to products that do not require a CKA.

Inform Tom of the outcome of the CKA and that Zenith cannot proceed to transact in the unlisted SIP on his behalf unless it also provides financial advisory services, and where applicable, provide such services.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because proceeding with opening a SIP trading account without considering the outcome of the CKA would not comply with the guidelines. (B) is a prudent action but not specifically required by the guidelines. (C) is incorrect because limiting trading to products that do not require a CKA does not address the lack of knowledge or experience in SIPs. (D) is correct because the guidelines require informing the client of the CKA outcome and that transactions in unlisted SIPs cannot proceed unless financial advisory services are provided, where applicable.

questions.q:
Evelyn, an advisor at Global Wealth Management ('Global' - and exempt financial advisor), is assisting her client, Carl, who wishes to diversify his investment portfolio by including unlisted SIPs. After completing a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA), it becomes clear that Carl does not have the necessary knowledge or experience to understand the complex features of unlisted SIPs. Carl, however, is insistent on proceeding with his investment plan.

What are Evelyn's obligations according to the guidelines for customers assessed not to possess knowledge or experience in derivatives or unlisted SIPs?
o: Open an unlisted SIP trading account for Carl, assuming that his insistence overrides the CKA outcome.

Inform Carl in writing of the outcome of the CKA, explain that Global cannot proceed to transact in the unlisted SIP on his behalf unless it also provides financial advisory services, and, where applicable, provide such services in accordance with the standards set out.
Advise Carl to only invest in listed SIPs or other simpler investment products where a CKA is not required.
Direct Carl to complete a specific educational program on unlisted SIPs and reassess his knowledge afterward.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because the advisor cannot disregard the CKA outcome based on the client's insistence. (B) is correct because it follows the guidelines that require informing the client of the CKA outcome and explaining that transactions in unlisted SIPs cannot proceed unless financial advisory services are provided, where applicable. (C) and (D) might be considered prudent advice but do not directly address the guidelines' requirements for handling situations where a client is assessed not to possess the necessary knowledge or experience in unlisted SIPs.

questions.q:
Jordan, a relationship manager at Prime Investments ('Prime'), is assisting a new client, Lisa, who is interested in trading exchange-listed Specified Investment Products (SIPs). Lisa is an experienced investor in stocks and bonds but has limited experience with SIPs. After conducting a Customer Account Review (CAR), Jordan finds that Lisa has the necessary knowledge and experience in derivatives to understand the risks involved with SIPs.

What steps should Jordan take next according to the guidelines for approval to open SIP trading accounts?
o: Immediately open a listed SIP trading account for Lisa based on her experience in stocks and bonds.
Seek Lisa's formal opt-in as an Accredited Investor before opening the trading account.
Provide Lisa with a statement in the account opening form that she can request for advice at any time concerning an SIP.
Recommend that Lisa focuses on investing in stocks and bonds only, as she has limited experience with SIPs.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because the decision to open an SIP trading account should be based on Lisa's understanding and experience with SIPs specifically, not just her experience with stocks and bonds. (B) is incorrect as it is not relevant in the context of SIP trading accounts. (C) is correct because providing advice on SIPs and ensuring that Lisa is aware she can request further advice at any time aligns with the guidelines for opening SIP trading accounts, ensuring clients are well-informed. (D) is incorrect because the guidelines encourage advisors to provide clients with the necessary information and support to make informed decisions about their investments, including SIPs, rather than limiting their options based on their initial experience level.

questions.q:
Sarah, an investment advisor at Global Finance Corp ('Global'), is reviewing the account of a long-standing client, Michael, who wishes to diversify his portfolio by investing in listed Specified Investment Products (SIPs). Michael has a solid understanding of equities but has never dealt with derivatives. Sarah conducts a Customer Account Review (CAR) and determines that Michael does not have the requisite knowledge or experience in derivatives. Michael is keen to proceed despite the results.

According to the guidelines for Customer Account Review and Customer Knowledge Assessment, which of the following steps should Sarah take?
o: Open a listed SIP trading account for Michael without any further action since he is a long-standing client.

Inform Michael of the CAR outcome and that he does not possess knowledge or experience in derivatives, obtain his written confirmation that he still intends to proceed, and provide him with a written statement explaining the general features and risks associated with investing in derivatives.
Recommend that Michael should only invest in equities since he lacks knowledge in derivatives.
Direct Michael to complete an online course on derivatives before reconsidering his request to invest in listed SIPs.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because the guidelines require advisors to inform clients about their CAR outcomes and the associated risks before proceeding with investments in SIPs, regardless of the client's history. (B) is correct as it aligns with the guidelines that mandate informing the client of the CAR outcome, obtaining written confirmation of their intention to proceed despite the lack of knowledge or experience, and providing an explanation of the risks involved in investing in derivatives. (C) and (D) are incorrect because the guidelines focus on ensuring the client is informed and consents to proceed after understanding the risks, rather than limiting investment options or mandating additional education as a prerequisite for investment.

questions.q:
Sophie, a compliance officer at Premier Investments ('Premier'), is conducting an internal audit to ensure that Premier's practices align with regulatory requirements, particularly in relation to their clients' investments in Specified Investment Products (SIPs). She notices that for several clients, detailed documentation of Customer Account Reviews (CARs) and Customer Knowledge Assessments (CKAs) is missing from their files.

According to the guidelines for documentation and record keeping, what is required of Premier to ensure compliance?
o: Premier should immediately cease all investment activities until all missing documentation is recovered or recreated.
Premier should ensure that all future CARs and CKAs are documented, but past omissions can be overlooked.
Premier must obtain and maintain detailed documentation for each CAR and CKA conducted, including information collected from clients and the outcomes of these assessments.
Premier should focus only on maintaining financial transaction records, as these are more critical for regulatory compliance.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because the guidelines require proper documentation but do not mandate ceasing all investment activities for past documentation omissions. (B) is incorrect because overlooking past omissions does not align with regulatory requirements for maintaining records. (C) is correct because the guidelines stipulate that CMS licence holders must document and maintain records of all CARs and CKAs, including client information and assessment outcomes, to ensure compliance. (D) is incorrect because, while financial transaction records are important, documentation of CARs and CKAs is also critical for regulatory compliance.

questions.q:
Hannah, an investment advisor at Global Assets Ltd., recently completed a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) for her client, Eric, who expressed an interest in investing in unlisted Specified Investment Products (SIPs). The CKA, conducted 13 months ago, assessed Eric as having the necessary knowledge and experience to understand the risks associated with unlisted SIPs. Eric now wishes to explore additional unlisted SIP investment opportunities.

What action should Hannah take according to the guidelines for the validity of the outcome of CKA before allowing Eric to proceed with new investments in unlisted SIPs?
o: Hannah should allow Eric to proceed with new investments in unlisted SIPs without any further action, as his previous CKA is still valid.
Hannah should conduct a new CKA for Eric, as the validity of the previous CKA has expired.
Hannah should review Eric's investment portfolio to ensure it aligns with his current knowledge and experience.
Hannah should inform Eric that he can only invest in listed SIPs until a new CKA is conducted.
questions.e: (A) is incorrect because the guidelines state that a new CKA must be conducted or relied upon if more than one year has elapsed since the last assessment. (B) is correct because the validity of a CKA lasts for one year, and since 13 months have passed, a new CKA is required before Eric can proceed with new investments in unlisted SIPs. (C) and (D) are prudent practices but do not directly address the guidelines regarding the validity period of a CKA.

questions.q:
During an internal review at Pinnacle Wealth Management ('Pinnacle'), it was discovered that client funds were being held in a trust account at a financial institution that recently lost its banking license. The management is concerned about the implications for compliance and client fund safety.

According to the guidelines for the maintenance of trust accounts with specified financial institutions, which of the following steps should Pinnacle take to rectify this situation?
o: Immediately transfer client funds to a trust account held at a bank licensed under the Banking Act.
Conduct a thorough due diligence on potential financial institutions before opening a new trust account.
Continue using the current financial institution for holding client funds until a suitable alternative is found.
Ensure that the new trust account is with a financial institution that is licensed, registered, or authorized to conduct banking business.
questions.e: (A), (B) and (D) are correct in accordance with the relevant guidelines that require that client funds must be held in trust accounts with specified financial institutions that are licensed, registered, or authorized to conduct banking business, and due diligence must be conducted before opening a new trust account. (C) is incorrect because continuing to use a financial institution that lost its banking license does not comply with the guidelines.

questions.q:
Jason, a portfolio manager at Elite Asset Management ('Elite'), is tasked with ensuring that all books and records are maintained accurately and in compliance with MAS regulations. He's particularly focused on ensuring that customer details and correspondence are properly documented and stored. Jason is aware that this is crucial not only for regulatory compliance but also for Elite's internal audit and risk management processes.

What specific records related to customer details and correspondence must Jason ensure are accurately maintained and stored at Elite?
o: Particulars of every customer and their guarantors.
Every written agreement entered into by Elite with its customers.
Every disclosure made to a customer under relevant regulations.
Every order prepared or received in the course of Elite's business.
questions.e: (A), (B), (C), and (D) are correct. Jason must ensure that particulars of every customer and their guarantors, all written agreements with customers, disclosures made under relevant regulations, and every order prepared or received are accurately maintained and stored, as these are essential for compliance with MAS regulations and for Elite's operational integrity. Incorrect options are not provided as all listed options are correct.

questions.q:
Lara, the operations manager at Global Derivatives Trading Corp ('Global Derivatives'), is overseeing the handling of customers' moneys and assets. She's aware of the stringent MAS regulations regarding the treatment of these funds and assets to protect customers' interests. Recently, Global Derivatives received a significant amount of money from a retail customer for OTC derivatives contracts. Lara wants to ensure that these funds are handled in strict compliance with MAS guidelines.

According to MAS regulations, what actions must Lara take to ensure compliance in handling the retail customer's moneys for OTC derivatives contracts?
o: Deposit all moneys received on account of the retail customer in a trust account.
Conduct initial and periodic due diligence on the suitability of the financial institution for its customers.
Give written notice to the financial institution and obtain acknowledgment that the moneys are held on trust.
Ensure that the retail customer's moneys are not commingled with other funds or used as margin for any transaction other than the customer's.
questions.e: (A), (B), (C), and (D) are correct. Lara must ensure that the retail customer's moneys for OTC derivatives contracts are deposited in a trust account, conduct due diligence on the financial institution, obtain acknowledgment that the funds are held on trust, and prevent commingling or misuse of the funds, in compliance with MAS regulations. Incorrect options are not provided as all listed options are correct.

questions.q:
Sarah, the CEO of Quantum Financial Services ('Quantum'), a CMS licence holder, is considering expanding the board of directors by adding two new members. One potential candidate, Alex, resides in Australia but plans to relocate to Singapore. Another candidate, Jordan, is a Singapore resident with extensive experience in capital markets. Sarah is aware of the regulatory requirements for board composition and residency but seeks clarity on the approval process for these appointments.

What steps must Sarah take to ensure compliance with the MAS regulations regarding the appointment of Alex and Jordan to Quantum's board of directors?
o: Obtain MAS' approval before appointing Alex as he is to reside in Singapore.
Inform MAS of Jordan's appointment as he is a resident in Singapore.
Obtain MAS' approval for changing the nature of the appointment if either director's role changes from non-executive to executive.
Ensure that both Alex and Jordan meet the "fit and proper" criteria as per MAS guidelines.
questions.e: (A), (B), (C), and (D) are correct. Quantum must obtain MAS' approval before appointing Alex since he plans to reside in Singapore and inform MAS about Jordan's appointment. Any changes from non-executive to executive roles require MAS' approval, and both must meet the "fit and proper" criteria. Incorrect options are not provided as all listed options are correct.

questions.q:
Mark, the marketing director at Global Investments Inc. ('Global'), is preparing an advertisement campaign for a new investment product. He wants to ensure the advertisements comply with MAS regulations. The campaign includes print ads, online banners, and an informational video. Mark is aware that the content must not be misleading and should provide a balanced view of the product. He plans to include a disclaimer that the advertisement has not been reviewed by MAS and to get the campaign materials approved by the senior management before publication.

What must Mark ensure to comply with MAS regulations for the advertisement campaign?
o: The product advertisement is not false or misleading.
The advertisement provides a fair and balanced view of the product.
The advertisement includes the statement: "This advertisement has not been reviewed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore."
The advertisement has been approved by a person specified in Regulation 46AA of the SFR(LCB) prior to its dissemination.
questions.e: (A), (B), (C), and (D) are correct. To comply with MAS regulations, Mark must ensure the advertisement is truthful, balanced, includes the required MAS disclaimer, and receives the appropriate internal approval before being published. Incorrect options are not provided as all listed options are correct.

questions.q:
Linda, a provisional representative at Vertex Advisory ('Vertex'), a CMS licence holder, has recently completed her CMFAS examinations and is eager to update her qualifications in the MAS Public Register of Representatives. She notifies her supervisor, who advises her on the next steps. Linda also recently changed her residential address.

What actions should Linda and Vertex take to comply with MAS regulations regarding Linda's status and personal particulars?
o: Vertex must notify MAS of Linda's change in qualification status within 14 days after the change.
Linda must inform Vertex of the change in her residential address within 7 days.
Ensure Linda's new qualifications are entered into the Public Register of Representatives on MAS' website.
Vertex should inform MAS if Linda ceases to act as a representative.
questions.e: (A), (B), and (C) are correct as Vertex must notify MAS of Linda's change in qualification within 14 days of the change, and Linda must inform Vertex of the change in her residential address within 7 days. (D) is correct as the principal must notify the MAS if its representative ceases to act as a representative.

questions.q:
Sophia, the head of client relations at Delta Capital Management ('Delta'), is reviewing the firm's procedures for documenting interactions with clients. She notes that while financial transaction confirmations are well-documented, there seems to be a gap in recording other forms of customer correspondence, such as the receipt of complaints and the provision of investment advice via email.

Based on the guidelines for customer correspondence, which types of documentation must Sophia ensure are comprehensively recorded and maintained by Delta to meet regulatory standards?
o: Every written agreement entered into by Delta with its customers.
Every disclosure made to a customer under relevant regulations.
Every report, letter, circular, memorandum, publication, advertisement, and other literature or advice distributed by Delta to any existing or prospective customer.
Every acknowledgment of a customer received under specific regulations, which shall be in prescribed forms.
questions.e: (A), (C), and (D) are correct because the guidelines require maintaining comprehensive records of all written agreements with customers, all forms of customer correspondence including disclosures, advice, and promotional materials, and any formal acknowledgments received from customers as per regulatory requirements. (B) is also required but was not specifically mentioned in the scenario as a gap identified by Sophia.

questions.q:
Prestige Investment Services ('Prestige') manages a large portfolio of client funds, including trust accounts holding client moneys. The firm's new CFO, Jonathan, is reviewing the procedures for withdrawing moneys from these trust accounts to ensure they align with regulatory requirements.

According to the guidelines, under which of the following conditions may Prestige withdraw moneys from a client's trust account?
o: To cover operational expenses of Prestige unrelated to client transactions.
To make a payment to another person entitled to the moneys as per the client's written direction.
To defray brokerage and other proper charges related to the client's transactions.
To invest in new financial products for Prestige's benefit.
questions.e: (B) and (C) are correct because the guidelines allow withdrawals from a client's trust account for making payments to those entitled to the moneys as per the client's written direction and to defray brokerage and other proper charges related to the client's transactions. (A) and (D) are incorrect as the guidelines prohibit using client moneys from trust accounts to cover operational expenses unrelated to client transactions or for investments for the firm's benefit.

questions.q:
Lighthouse Investment Services ('Lighthouse') is planning to open new trust accounts for depositing client moneys. The management wants to ensure that the chosen financial institutions align with regulatory requirements and the firm's commitment to client fund safety.

What actions must Lighthouse take according to the guidelines for assessing the suitability of specified financial institutions for maintaining trust accounts?
o: Choose financial institutions based solely on the highest interest rates offered for trust accounts.
Conduct initial and periodic due diligence on the financial institutions' suitability for holding client funds.
Ensure that the chosen financial institutions are licensed, registered, or authorized to conduct banking business in their jurisdiction.
Select financial institutions based on convenience of location to Lighthouse's offices.
questions.e: (B) and (C) are correct because the guidelines require conducting initial and periodic due diligence on the suitability of financial institutions for holding client funds and ensuring that these institutions are properly licensed, registered, or authorized to conduct banking business. (A) and (D) are incorrect as they do not align with the guidelines' emphasis on safety, regulatory compliance, and due diligence over factors like interest rates and location convenience.

questions.q:
During an internal compliance review at Orion Financial Services ('Orion'), the compliance officer, Mark, discovered that the records for several clients lacked comprehensive details. Specifically, the records were missing particulars of authorized traders for these clients and detailed information on each customer asset, including the description and date of deposit.

According to the guidelines for keeping books and records, which of the following details must Mark ensure are included in Orion's client records to comply with regulatory requirements?
o: Particulars of every customer and their guarantors.
Particulars of authorized traders for the clients.
A detailed description of each customer asset, including the date of deposit.
The name of custodians with whom Orion deposits customer monies and assets.
questions.e: (B) and (C) are correct because the guidelines specify that CMS licence holders must keep records that include particulars of authorized traders and a detailed description of each customer asset, including the date of deposit. (A) is also required but was not the focus of the discrepancy found by Mark. (D) is important for compliance but not directly related to the missing information identified by Mark.

questions.q:
Vertex Asset Management ('Vertex') is reviewing its procedures for withdrawing assets from custody accounts on behalf of its clients. The firm wants to ensure that these withdrawals are in strict compliance with regulatory guidelines to maintain trust and integrity.

According to the guidelines, under which conditions may Vertex withdraw assets from a client's custody account?
o: Vertex may withdraw assets to cover unexpected operational expenses.
Vertex is allowed to withdraw assets for making payments to another person entitled to the assets as per the client's written direction.
Vertex can withdraw assets to invest in high-risk ventures if it believes the returns will benefit the client.
Vertex may withdraw assets to defray brokerage and other proper charges related to the client's transactions.
questions.e: (B) and (D) are correct because the guidelines allow withdrawals from a client's custody account for the purpose of making payments to those entitled to the assets as per the client's written direction and to defray brokerage and other proper charges related to the client's transactions. (A) and (C) are incorrect as they do not align with the regulatory guidelines that restrict the withdrawal of assets from custody accounts to specific, client-directed purposes.

questions.q:
Horizon Financial Planners ('Horizon') specializes in advising retail customers on a wide range of investment opportunities. The firm is revising its policies to ensure that the handling of retail customers' moneys strictly adheres to regulatory guidelines.

According to the guidelines, which of the following practices must Horizon follow when dealing with moneys received from retail customers?
o: Use the moneys to grant loans to other clients or to Horizon itself.
Deposit the moneys into a trust account unless the moneys are to be used immediately for a transaction authorized by the customer.
Invest the moneys in high-yield corporate bonds to generate returns for the firm.
Ensure that any investment of the moneys is in accordance with the customer's written instructions or consent.
questions.e: (B) and (D) are correct because the guidelines mandate that moneys received from retail customers must be deposited into a trust account unless they are to be used immediately for a transaction authorized by the customer, and any investment of these moneys must align with the customer's written instructions or consent. (A) and (C) are incorrect as using client moneys to grant loans or investing in high-yield corporate bonds without specific consent does not comply with the guidelines for handling retail customers' moneys.

questions.q:
Quantum Financial Advisors ('Quantum') has decided to open a new trust account for client moneys with TrustBank, a well-regarded bank. To comply with regulatory requirements, Quantum needs to ensure proper documentation and acknowledgment from TrustBank regarding the nature of the trust account.

According to the guidelines, which of the following must Quantum do to comply with the notification and acknowledgment requirements from specified financial institutions?
o: Assume that TrustBank understands the regulatory requirements for trust accounts and proceed without formal acknowledgment.

Obtain written acknowledgment from TrustBank that the account is designated as a trust account and that TrustBank cannot exercise any right of set-off against the moneys for any debt owed by Quantum to TrustBank.
Ensure that TrustBank provides a verbal confirmation that they recognize the account as a trust account.
Send a written notice to TrustBank specifying that the moneys deposited are held on trust for Quantum's clients.
questions.e: (B) and (D) are correct because the guidelines require CMS licence holders to send a written notice to the financial institution specifying that the moneys are held on trust for the clients and to obtain a written acknowledgment from the institution that recognizes the account as a trust account and restricts the institution from exercising any right of set-off against the moneys for debts owed by the CMS licence holder. (A) and (C) are incorrect as assumptions and verbal confirmations do not meet the regulatory requirements for documentation and acknowledgment.

questions.q:
Alliance Capital Management ('Alliance') is reviewing its policies on investing moneys received on account of customers. The firm wants to ensure that its investment strategies for these moneys are in full compliance with regulatory guidelines.

According to the guidelines, in which of the following forms of investment is Alliance permitted to hold moneys received on account of its customers?
o: In highly speculative stock options offering the potential for high returns.
In any Government securities or debt instruments of the government of the country of an organised market where Alliance normally transacts its business.
In private equity funds with a proven track record of performance.
In real estate investment trusts (REITs) listed on major stock exchanges.
questions.e: (B) is correct because the guidelines allow for the investment of client moneys in safe and relatively low-risk instruments such as Government securities or debt instruments of the government of the country of an organized market. (A), (C) and (D) are incorrect as speculative stock options, private equity funds, and listed REITs do not align with the guidelines' emphasis on safety and risk management for client moneys.

questions.q:
Vertex Securities ('Vertex') deals extensively in capital markets products and often deposits client moneys with clearing houses and members of clearing facilities to facilitate transactions. The compliance officer wants to ensure that these practices align with regulatory guidelines.

According to the guidelines, under what circumstances is Vertex allowed to deposit client moneys with a clearing house or members of a clearing facility?
o: Only if the client provides explicit consent for each transaction involving their moneys.
For the purpose of facilitating positions and transactions in capital markets products traded, entered, settled, or cleared on such entities.
If it is more convenient for Vertex to manage client transactions through these entities.
When the clearing house offers better interest rates on deposits compared to banks.
questions.e: (B) is correct because the guidelines permit the deposit of client moneys with a clearing house or members of a clearing facility for the specific purpose of facilitating positions and transactions in capital markets products. (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect as the guidelines focus on the purpose of facilitating transactions rather than client consent for each transaction, convenience, or interest rates.

questions.q:
Quantum Brokers ('Quantum') specializes in trading derivatives for its clients and often needs to deposit clients' assets with clearing houses to facilitate these transactions. The firm's operations team is ensuring that their practices align with regulatory guidelines.

According to the guidelines, under what circumstances is Quantum allowed to deposit clients' assets with a clearing house or members of a clearing facility?
o: Quantum can deposit clients' assets with a clearing house only if it results in higher returns for Quantum.
Quantum is allowed to deposit clients' assets with a clearing house for the purpose of facilitating positions and transactions in derivatives contracts.
Quantum should deposit clients' assets with a clearing house only when the clearing house is located in the same country as Quantum.
Quantum can deposit clients' assets with any clearing house or member of a clearing facility based on the preference of Quantum's management.
questions.e: (B) is correct because the guidelines permit the deposit of clients' assets with a clearing house or members of a clearing facility specifically for the purpose of facilitating positions and transactions in derivatives contracts. (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect as they do not comply with the regulatory guidelines that focus on the purpose of facilitating transactions rather than returns, location preferences, or management preferences.

questions.q:
Upon receiving a significant transfer of securities from a new client, Apex Wealth Management ('Apex') realizes that it needs to ensure proper handling and documentation of these assets to comply with regulatory standards.

According to the guidelines for duties of CMS licence holders upon receipt of customers' assets, which of the following actions must Apex take?
o: Apex must immediately use the securities for its own investment purposes to demonstrate asset management capabilities.
Apex must deposit the client's securities in a custody account held on trust for the client and ensure that the client's assets are not commingled with any other assets.
Apex should wait for the client to provide specific instructions before taking any action with the received securities.
Apex must sell the securities if they believe the market is about to decline to protect the client's investment.
questions.e: (B) is correct because the guidelines require that CMS licence holders must deposit the client's assets in a custody account held on trust for the client and ensure segregation from other assets. (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect as they do not align with the regulatory requirements for handling and safeguarding clients' assets upon receipt.

questions.q:
Falcon Wealth Advisors ('Falcon') has received a substantial amount of assets from a retail client, intending to use them as collateral for the client's trades. Falcon's compliance officer reviews the firm's policies to ensure adherence to regulatory guidelines regarding such assets.

According to the guidelines, what must Falcon do when dealing with assets received from a retail customer for use as collateral?
o: Falcon can immediately sell the assets to fund its own investments if it deems the market conditions favorable.
Falcon must enter into an agreement with the retail client setting out the terms for the use of the assets as collateral.
Falcon should use the assets for internal purposes as long as it benefits the overall client portfolio.
Falcon can decide to lend the assets to another client without the retail client's consent.
questions.e: (B) is correct because the guidelines require that CMS licence holders must enter into an agreement with the client that clearly sets out the terms for the use of the client's assets as collateral. (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect as they do not comply with the regulatory guidelines that mandate client consent and clear terms for the use of assets received from retail customers.

questions.q:
Evan, the compliance officer at Secure Futures Brokerage ('Secure Futures'), is reviewing the monthly and quarterly statements sent to clients to ensure they meet the requirements set by MAS. He notices that for some clients who are accredited investors, statements have not been sent for the last quarter because these clients opted out of receiving them. Evan wants to confirm that this practice aligns with MAS regulations and that Secure Futures is not in breach of any requirements regarding the provision of statements to clients.

What conditions must be met for Secure Futures to not send monthly statements to accredited investors according to MAS regulations?
o: The information to be contained in the statement has already been sent by CDP to the customer.
Periodic reconciliation is performed between transactions and positions held by Secure Futures and its clients.
The accredited investor has requested, in writing, not to receive such monthly statements.
Real-time electronic statements have been made available to the accredited investor, and they have agreed to use these electronic statements.
questions.e: (B), (C), and (D) are correct. Secure Futures does not need to send a monthly statement if periodic reconciliation is performed, if the accredited investor has opted out in writing, or if real-time electronic statements are provided and agreed upon. (A) is also correct in this context.

questions.q:
In an effort to secure a loan for expanding its operations, Elite Investments ('Elite') considers using its clients' assets as collateral. Before proceeding, the management team seeks to understand the regulatory implications of such an action.

According to the guidelines for the mortgage of customer's assets, under which conditions may Elite mortgage its clients' assets?
o: Elite may mortgage clients' assets without notifying the clients if the market conditions are unfavorable.
Elite can mortgage clients' assets if the action is expected to yield financial benefits for Elite.
Elite must obtain the clients' written consent before mortgaging their assets and ensure the sum does not exceed the amount owed by the clients to Elite.
Elite should mortgage clients' assets only for short-term loans to quickly improve its liquidity.
questions.e: (C) is correct because the guidelines specify that CMS licence holders must obtain the clients' written consent before mortgaging their assets and the mortgage amount must not exceed the amount owed by the clients to the CMS licence holder. (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect as they do not align with the regulatory requirements that prioritize client consent and limit the conditions under which clients' assets may be mortgaged.

questions.q:
Sterling Financial Services ('Sterling') is reviewing its policies for maintaining custody accounts for its clients' assets. The firm wants to ensure that these accounts are maintained with custodians that meet regulatory requirements and offer the highest level of security for their clients' assets.

According to the guidelines for the maintenance of custody accounts with specified custodians, which of the following steps should Sterling take?
o: Sterling must ensure that the custody accounts are maintained with institutions that have a high social media rating.
Sterling should maintain custody accounts with any institution offering the lowest fees, regardless of their licensing status.
Sterling must maintain custody accounts with institutions that are licensed, registered, or authorized to act as custodians in their jurisdiction.
Sterling should prioritize convenience and maintain custody accounts with local institutions, regardless of their specific custodial capabilities.
questions.e: (C) is correct because the guidelines stipulate that CMS licence holders must maintain custody accounts with specified custodians that are properly licensed, registered, or authorized to act as custodians in their jurisdiction. (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect as they do not align with the regulatory requirements for selecting custodians based on their licensing status, security of clients' assets, and regulatory compliance, rather than social media ratings, fees, or convenience.

questions.q: A CMS licence lapses if the holder does not commence business in at least one of the regulated activities to which the licence pertains within ____ from the date of the grant of the licence.
o: 1 month
3 months
6 months
1 year
questions.e: (SFR (LCB) - July 2021) A CMS licence lapses if the holder does not commence business in at least one of the regulated activities to which the licence pertains within 6 months from the date of the grant of the licence.

questions.q: A Boutique Corporate Finance Advisor (BCF) is required to maintain a base capital of minimum ____.
o: S$5 million
S$1 million
questions.e: A Boutique Corporate Finance Advisor (BCF) is required to maintain a base capital of minimum S$5 million.

questions.q: PQR corporation is a member of a securities exchange and is NOT an introducing broker or restricted broker in relation to dealing in securities. PQR is authorised to trade on all contracts listed on the SGX-ST. PQR is likely to be a:
o: Non-clearing member
Clearing member
Non-Member
Trading Member
questions.e: A clearing member refers to a corporation which is a member of an approved clearing house authorised to operate a clearing facility for securities. A non-clearing member refers to a corporation (not being an introducing broker or restricted broker in relation to dealing in securities) which is a member of a securities exchange. A non-member refers to a corporation (not being an introducing broker or restricted broker in relation to dealing in securities) which is not a member of a securities exchange.

questions.q: A CMS Licence holder (licensee) CANNOT divulge any information related to a customer order:
o: Unless the disclosure can help increase the profits of the client.
Unless the disclosure can help increase the profits of the licensee.
Unless it is required by MAS.
None of the above.
questions.e: A CMS Licence holder (licensee) CANNOT divulge any information related to a customer order unless, inter-alia, it is required by the MAS.

questions.q: For which of the following purposes the CMS licence holder (licensee) is authorised to withdraw the assets of its customer from the custody account?
o: For securities lending.
For transferring assets to any person entitled for such transfer.
For meeting obligations of the customer regarding leveraged foreign exchange trading.
All of the above.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder (licensee) is authorised to withdraw the assets of its customer from the custody account for all the given purposes.

questions.q: Under which of the following circumstances a CMS licence holder (licensee) may hypothecate the assets of customers?
o: If there is prior written agreement with the customer.
The sum of the claims on the assets due to such hypothecation does not exceed the amount owed by the customer to the licensee.
The claim to which each customer's assets are subject due to the hypothecation does not exceed the amount owed by the customer to the licensee.
All of the above.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder (licensee) may hypothecate the assets of customers in all the given circumstances.

questions.q: With which of the following entities is a CMS Licence holder allowed to maintain a trust account for depositing moneys received from customers?
o: A licensed custodian outside Singapore, if the money is denominated in foreign currency.
A bank licensed under the Banking Act.
Any merchant bank.
A finance company licensed under the Finance Companies Act.
questions.e: A CMS Licence holder is NOT allowed to maintain a trust account for depositing moneys received from customers with ANY merchant bank. It may do so with a merchant bank APPROVED as a financial institution under the MAS Act. It may also do so with a licensed custodian outside Singapore if the money is denominated in a foreign currency, a bank licensed under the Banking Act or a finance company licenced under the Finance Companies Act.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder must inform MAS within ____ if it ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licensed for.
o: 7 days
14 days
21 days
30 days
questions.e: A CMS licence holder is required to inform MAS within 14 days of any change in particulars if it ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licenced for, or if there is a change in the CMS licence holder's record.

questions.q: In which of the following forms can a CMS licence holder (licensee) hold moneys received from customers on trust?
o: Government securities.
Debt instrument of the government of the country where the licensee normally operates.
Any other securities authorised by the relevant authority.
All of the above.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder may hold moneys received from customers on trust in any of the given forms.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Approval to Open SIP Trading Accounts for a customer is TRUE?
o: For opening a trading account for unlisted SIP, approval of the MAS must be obtained.
For opening a trading account for listed SIP, approval of independent senior management personnel of the trading member is required.
If the outcome of the CKA is positive, approval of an independent senior management personnel of the trading member is NOT required.
If the outcome of the CAR is negative, approval of the MAS is required.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder must not open a SIP trading account for a customer unless its senior management who is not involved in that account's opening process and is not a connected person of that customer is satisfied, on the basis of the outcome of the CAR or CKA, that the customer has knowledge or experience in derivatives (for CAR) or in the unlisted SIP (for CKA), and has approved the opening of the customer's SIP trading account. Therefore, even if the outcome of the CAR or CKA is positive, approval of an independent senior management personnel is required.

questions.q: LMN (a trading member) executed a trade for its client John on 3 January (Monday). The vital details about the trade became available on 5 January. LMN must send the contract note for the trade to John latest by: (presume Jan 3 to Jan 7 are market days and business days)
o: 4 Jan
5 Jan
6 Jan
7 Jan
questions.e: A CMS licence holder must send its customer a contract note for the purchase or sale of securities or futures contracts by the next market day. In cases where any detail about the transaction which needs to be included in the contract note only becomes available later, the CMS licence holder should issue the contract note by the next business day after the detail becomes available. Since the details become available on 05 Jan, the contract note must be issued by 06 Jan.

questions.q: Which of the following information must be kept by a CMS licence holder regarding its proprietary transactions?
o: The name of the counterparty to the transaction.
Fee arising from transactions.
Unrealised gains.
All of the above.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder should retain particulars of every proprietary transaction, including the description and quantity of the assets the price and fee arising from the transaction, the transaction date and settlement or delivery date, the name of the counterparty to the transaction, and the realised or unrealised gain or loss.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the grant of Capital Markets Services (CMS) Licence is TRUE?
o: It can be granted only to an individual.
It can be granted only to a corporation.
It can be granted to an individual or a corporation.
It can be granted to anyone, including a body unincorporate.
questions.e: A CMS licence is only be granted to a corporation.

questions.q: For which of the following reasons a CMS licence holder (licensee) CANNOT advance his money to the trust account of the customer?
o: For preventing the balance from going below the minimum margin.
For preventing the account from being under-funded.
For taking advantage of an investment opportunity for which there is insufficient balance in the account of the customer.
None of the above.
questions.e: A licensee CANNOT advance his money to the trust account of a customer for taking advantage of an investment opportunity for which there is insufficient balance in the account of the customer. It can do so to prevent the account from being under-margined or under-funded.

questions.q: A Capital Markets Services Licence holder (licensee) may withdraw customer's money from a trust account for the purpose of:
o: Reimbursing the licensee any money it has advanced to the account.
Reimbursing the licensee any interest that it is entitled to even if the account becomes under-funded.
Meeting the expenses it has incurred in the course of servicing the customer's account.
Making a payment to any account directed by the customer in writing.
questions.e: A licensee may withdraw customer's money from a trust account for reimbursing the licensee any money it has advanced to the account and making a payment to any account directed by the customer in writing. It cannot withdraw the money if the withdrawal leads to the account becoming under-funded. It cannot do so for meeting the expenses it has incurred in the course of servicing the customer's account.

questions.q: A Member is required to deposit customer's monies and assets in the relevant account no later than ____ after receipt?
o: The next business day.
Two business days.
Three business days.
Seven business days.
questions.e: A Member shall deposit customer moneys into a trust account or other account directed by the customer, no later than the next business day after receiving the monies.

questions.q: When does a Trading Member need to send quarterly statements of accounts to its customers?
o: If there's been a change in the customer's account in March, June, September and December as compared to the relevant previous months.
If a monthly statement has not been sent for the last month of the calendar quarter.
If the customer trades infrequently during the quarter.
If the total value of the customer's trades during the quarter is below SGD 20,000.
questions.e: A monthly statement need not be sent to a customer if there has been no change in the customer's account in the month compared to the previous month. Otherwise, it must be sent. Therefore, if there's been a change in the customer's account in March, June, September and December as compared to the relevant previous months, a monthly statement must be sent. If a monthly statement has been sent, a quarterly statement NEED NOT be sent. Therefore, option A is incorrect. If a monthly statement has not been sent for the last month of a calendar quarter (i.e., March, June, September and December), the CMS licence holder shall send a quarterly statement to the customer, containing the same information that is required on a monthly statement of account. Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.q: If a representative informs his principal company that he has changed his residential address, the principal company must notify MAS about the change within how many days?
o: 7 days of the change.
14 days of the change.
21 days of the change.
30 days of the change.
questions.e: A principal company is required to notify MAS of its representative's change of particulars no later than 14 days after the date of the change of the particulars in the prescribed form and manner.

questions.q: According to the MAS Notice on Sale of Investment Products (SFA 04-N12), which of the following are transactions in overseas-listed investment products?
o: The purchase of any overseas-listed investment product OTHER THAN in connection with the creation of short positions.
The sale of any overseas-listed investment product in connection with the creation of short positions.
Expressing an interest to purchase an overseas-listed investment product.
Putting up a margin to sell an overseas-listed investment product.
questions.e: According to the MAS Notice on Sale of Investment Products (SFA 04-N12, Paragraph 29F), "transact" means (a) The purchase of any overseas-listed investment product other than in connection with the creation of short positions; or (b) The sale of any overseas-listed investment product in connection with the creation of short positions.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Representative Notification Framework (RNF) is FALSE?
o: Financial institutions can register representatives as temporary representatives with MAS through the RNF.
All representatives are assigned a unique number under RNF which changes only if they change principals.
Members of the public may verify the representatives by using the RNF.
None of the above.
questions.e: All representatives are assigned a unique representative number. The number STAYS the same even if a representative changes his principal. The other statements are true.

questions.q: On receipt of assets from a customer, a CMS licence holder (licensee):
o: Should ensure that the assets are not commingled with any other assets.
May commingle the assets of the customer with assets of another customer and deposit them in the same account.
Should make arrangements for a custodian to maintain the custody account.
All of the above.
questions.e: All the given statements are true.

questions.q: If a provisional representative changes his residential address, he must inform his principal within ____ after the date of change.
o: 3 days
1 day
10 days
None of the above.
questions.e: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform his principal company of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change of the particulars.

questions.q: XYZ Bank conducts the regulated activity of dealing in securities in Singapore. XYZ wants to conduct the regulated activity of advising on corporate finance. In this context, which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: XYZ must obtain a CMS Licence for advising on corporate finance.
XYZ cannot advise on corporate finance because it is a bank.
XYZ can only advise its related corporations on corporate finance.
XYZ need not meet the Base Capital Requirements (BCR) for Dealing in Securities.
questions.e: Any bank licensed under the Banking Act (Cap. 19) is exempt from the requirement to hold a CMSL to carry on business in any regulated activity (under section 99 of the SFA, Banks are exempt institutions). Advising on corporate finance is a regulated activity and XYZ can conduct such an activity without obtaining a CMSL. XYZ need not meet the BCR for dealing in securities because it is not required to obtain a CMSL for dealing in securities.

questions.q: Which of the following entities CANNOT be appointed as a custodian for the assets of a customer by a CMS licence holder?
o: An approved trustee for a collective investment scheme.
Any firm that provides brokerage services in relation to securities.
Any other person licensed under the Act to provide custodial services for securities.
All of the above.
questions.e: Any firm that provides brokerage services in relation to securities CANNOT be appointed a custodian for the assets of a customer by a CMS licensee.

questions.q: The public register of representatives contains details of the principal companies with which the representative has worked for within the past ____.
o: 3 years
2 years
10 years
7 years
questions.e: Besides the name of the representative, the regulated activities which the representative is allowed to conduct, the principal companies which the representative has worked for within the past three years, and any formal regulatory action taken by MAS against the representative, would be displayed on the Public Register of Representatives.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Customer Account Review (CAR) conducted before opening a SIP trading account is TRUE?
o: CAR is performed for unlisted SIPs.
CAR is not performed in the case of retail customers.
CAR does not take into account the work experience of the customer.
CAR takes into account the educational qualifications of the customer.
questions.e: CAR is performed for LISTED SIPs. It IS performed for retail customers. It CONSIDERS the educational qualifications and the work experience of the customer.

questions.q: PQR Limited is the auditor of LMN Limited (a trading member of the SGX-ST). PQR discovers certain issues while conducting the audit of LMN's accounts. PQR should immediately send a report in writing to MAS and the SGX-ST if the issues:
o: materially impact the financial soundness of LMN.
relate to fraud or dishonesty.
concern violation of the SFA.
relate to clerical errors in the footnotes to the accounts.
questions.e: Clerical errors in the footnotes to the accounts are likely to be minor issues. Serious issues, such as those mentioned in options A, B and C, and irregularities that may affect or jeopardise the moneys or assets of any customer of the CMS licence holder, must be reported.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder must not open a listed Specified Investment Products (SIPs) trading account for a customer unless its senior management has approved the opening of the account. The senior management should:-
o: Not be a connected person of the customer.
Not be involved in the particular account opening process.
Base its approval on the Customer Account Review or the Customer Knowledge Assessment, as the case may be.
All of the above.
questions.e: CMS licence holder must not open a listed SIP trading account for a customer unless its senior management, who is not involved in that particular account opening process and is not a connected person of that customer, is satisfied based on the outcome of the CAR or CKA that the customer has knowledge or experience in derivatives (for CAR) or in the unlisted SIPs (for CKA), and has approved the opening of the customer's listed SIP trading account.

questions.q: OPQ is a Capital Markets Services (CMS) licence holder for dealing in capital markets products. John has been working for OPQ for 9 months. John executes trades for OPQ's clients through its portal. In this context, which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: OPQ must be licensed and regulated under the FAA.
John is required to be an appointed representative under the SFA.
OPQ can conduct any regulated activity under the second schedule of the SFA based on its CMS licence.
OPQ must renew its CMS licence every year in order to continue operations.
questions.e: CMS licence holders are licensed and regulated under the SFA (NOT FAA). A corporation may make an application for a CMS licence to carry on business in one or more of the regulated activities as specified in the SFA. A CMSL holder must carry on business only in the regulated activity for which it is licensed (each licence is specific to a regulated activity). Individuals acting for CMS licence holders to carry out the regulated activities are required to be appointed representatives under the SFA. A CMSL need not be renewed. It may lapse, or be revoked or suspended by the MAS, under certain conditions.

questions.q: In case of Overseas-Listed Investment Products, exempt financial advisers are required to provide a risk warning statement to the retail customers and obtain an acknowledgement of the statement from the customer. The acknowledgement has to be retained for ____.
o: One year.
2 years.
5 years.
10 years.
questions.e: CMS licence holders or exempt financial institutions must maintain records of the customer's acknowledgement for a period of not less than 5 years.

questions.q: Which of the following are examples of LISTED Specified Investment Products (SIPs)?
o: All unit trusts
All ILPs
Structured notes
Exchange-Traded Notes
questions.e: Examples of SIPs Listed on an Exchange include Certain exchange traded funds and notes, Structured warrants, Futures, and Certificates. Examples of SIPs NOT Listed on an Exchange include Structured notes (e.g., equity-linked structured notes, credit linked structured notes), Certain unit trusts, and Certain investment-linked life insurance policies.

questions.q: For deciding whether to grant a CMS licence to an applicant, the MAS assesses the track record of the applicant at least for the last ____.
o: 5 years
10 years
3 years
2 years
questions.e: For deciding whether to grant a CMS licence to an applicant, the MAS assesses the track record of the applicant at least for the last 5 years.

questions.q: John and Jane intend to open a joint Specified Investment Products (SIPs) Trading Account with Trading Member PQR (a CMSL Licence holder). In this context, which of the following statements about Customer Account Review (CAR) & Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) is/are TRUE?
o: If John and Jane intend to open a joint LISTED SIP trading account, CAR may be conducted on either John or Jane.
If John and Jane intend to open a joint UNLISTED SIP trading account, CKA must be conducted on both John and Jane.
If John and Jane do not provide information on their work experience, they will be deemed to not possess knowledge or experience in SIPs for CKA and CAR.
If John and Jane fail the CAR assessment, PQR MUST NOT open their joint trading account.
questions.e: For joint trading accounts, the requirement to conduct the CAR or CKA will apply to EACH of the customers (NOT EITHER) intending to open the joint SIP trading account. For the purpose of the CAR and CKA, if a customer does not provide the relevant information, he shall be deemed as not possessing the required knowledge or experience in SIPs. If the customer intends to proceed to open a LISTED SIP trading despite failing the CAR assessment, the CMSL may open the account after suitably informing the customer of the risks involved and obtaining his written confirmation.

questions.q: Which of the following information is required to be obtained by a Member for opening an account for an individual customer who wishes to trade in shares of listed companies?
o: Details of who his employer is.
Whether he is an undischarged bankrupt.
His investment objectives.
All of the above
questions.e: For opening an account for an individual customer who wishes to trade in shares of listed companies, a Member must, inter-alia, obtain details of who his employer is, whether he is an undischarged bankrupt, and his investment objectives.

questions.q: MiddleMan corporation is an introducing broker dealing in securities. MiddleMan:
o: May carry customer's positions in its books.
May not carry customer's margins or accounts in its books.
May solicit or accept orders for purchase or sale of any securities from a restricted broker.
May accept money from any customer as settlement of any contract for purchase of securities by that customer.
questions.e: For the purposes of dealing in securities, an introducing broker refers to a corporation (dealing in securities) which does not carry any customer's positions, margins or accounts in its own books; and either (i) carries on the business only of soliciting or accepting orders for the purchase or sale of any securities from any customer (NOT BEING A restricted broker); or (ii) accepts money or assets from any customer as settlement of, or a margin for, or to guarantee or secure, any contract for the purchase or sale of securities by that customer.

questions.q: What is the validity of a positive outcome of a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA)?
o: 1 year.
2 years.
5 years.
3 years.
questions.e: If a customer is assessed to have knowledge or experience to transact in an unlisted SIP, the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution may allow the customer to transact the unlisted SIP for a period of one year from the date of the assessment.

questions.q: Under which of the following circumstances a CMS licence holder (licensee) is NOT required to provide a quarterly statement of account to a customer?
o: If the monthly statement has been sent to the customer for the last month of the calendar quarter.
If there are only a few transactions during the first calendar month of the quarter.
If the licensee considers it unnecessary to send the quarterly statement.
If the investor does not take active interest in the trades.
questions.e: If a monthly statement has not been sent for the last month of a calendar quarter (i.e., March, June, September and December), the CMS licence holder shall send a quarterly statement to the customer, containing the same information that is required on a monthly statement of account. Otherwise, he need not send the quarterly statement.

questions.q: If an appointed representative has ceased to act as a representative for a continuous period of ____, his status ceases even if his principal has not notified the MAS about the fact that he has ceased to act as a representative.
o: 14 days
21 days
one month
3 months
questions.e: If an appointed representative has ceased to act as a representative for a continuous period of one month, his status ceases even if his principal has not notified the MAS about the fact that he has ceased to act as a representative.

questions.q: Jane approaches LMN (a CMSL holder) for opening a trading account for LISTED SIPs. Jane is assessed not to possess the required knowledge or experience in trading in derivatives based on a Customer Account Review (CAR). LMN informs Jane about the outcome of the CAR but Jane insists on opening an account to trade in Listed SIPs. LMN:
o: should not open the SIP trading account for Jane.
may open the SIP trading account for Jane if she agrees to put up a suitable additional margin for each trade.
must obtain at least a verbal confirmation from Jane that she intends to open the account despite the negative outcome.
may explain the risks associated with derivatives to her in writing.
questions.e: If Jane intends to proceed to open an SIP trading account despite the negative outcome of the CAR, LMN must inform her in writing of the outcome of the CAR, obtain her written confirmation that he still intends to proceed with the opening of the SIP despite the not having the required knowledge or experience, explain to her the general features and risks associated with investing in derivatives and provide her a written statement of the explanation given, and inform her in writing that it is her responsibility to ensure that she understands any capital markets product(s) that she intends to transact using the SIP trading account.

questions.q: In which of the following cases an applicant for a CMS licence may be considered fit and proper?
o: He assumes concurrent responsibilities giving rise to a conflict of interest.
He has fully satisfied a judgement debt in Singapore.
He has failed to meet his financial obligations on several occasions.
None of the above.
questions.e: If the applicant has FULLY SATISFIED the judgement debt, he will be considered fit and proper. He will not be considered fit and proper based on the competence and capability criteria if he assumes concurrent responsibilities giving rise to a conflict of interest. He will fail the financial soundness test of fitness and propriety if he has failed to meet his financial obligations on several occasions.

questions.q: OPQ Limited is the auditor of XYZ Limited (a trading member of the SGX-ST). OPQ discovers certain serious irregularities while conducting the audit of XYZ's accounts. OPQ does not send a report to MAS and the SGX-ST about the irregularities. In this context, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
o: The MAS must request XYZ to send the auditor's report on the irregularities.
The MAS must summon the CEO of XYZ.
The MAS may appoint an auditor to examine and audit the books of XYZ.
The SGX-ST may appoint an auditor to examine and audit the books of XYZ.
questions.e: If the CMSL holder does not submit the required accounts or reports to the MAS, or the auditor does not send a report on material irregularities to the MAS, the MAS may appoint an auditor to carry out an examination and audit of the CMS licence holder's books.

questions.q: Under the SGX-ST rules on confidentiality of customer's information, a Trading Member and its Trading Representative may disclose customer information to another person if it is for the effective execution of the customer's order. The person who receives such information:
o: may disclose the information to anyone else if he deems necessary.
may not further disclose the information.
may further disclose the information to employees of the Trading Member.
may further disclose the information if permitted by the Trading Representative.
