questions.e: If the disclosure is for the effective execution of the customer's order or the disclosure is necessary for the operations and risk management of the Trading Member (if these functions have been outsourced), then the person receiving the information must not disclose the information to anyone else.

questions.q: BigShot is a Trading Member (TM). BigShot wants to appoint John as a TEMPORARY Representative to deal in shares. Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for John's appointment as a Temporary Representative?
o: John must possess the same educational qualifications as required for appointed representatives.
John must pass the relevant exams, as required by appointed representatives.
John must be working for a related entity of BigShot.
John must be currently licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated for the regulated activity in any overseas jurisdiction.
questions.e: In addition to education and work experience-related admission criteria, Temporary representatives must be an employee of a related entity of the principal and must be currently licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated for that activity in an overseas jurisdiction with a regulatory regime that is COMPARABLE to that of Singapore (NOT ANY OVERSEAS JURISDICTION). Temporary representatives need not meet the relevant examination requirements. They are appointed for a short period.

questions.q: In relation to a CMS licence holder, the term customer does not include:
o: The licensee transacting on its own account.
An officer of the licensee.
A representative of the licensee.
A related corporation of the licensee if the account belongs to and is maintained wholly for the benefit of that related corporation.
questions.e: In relation to a CMS licence holder, the term customer does not include any of the given entities or persons.

questions.q: In the context of segregation of customer's monies and assets and fiduciary obligations, a 'customer' DOES NOT include:
o: A CMS license holder carrying out a regulated activity on his own account.
An Approved Trader of the Member.
A related corporation of the Member.
A Registered Representative of the CMS Licence holder.
questions.e: In this context, the term Customer DOES NOT include the CMS licence holder carrying out any regulated activity for its own account, a director, officer, employee, Approved Trader or Registered Representative of the CMS licence holder or Member, or a related corporation of the CMS licence holder or Member with respect to an account belonging to and maintained wholly for the benefit of that related corporation.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are NOT considered money received on account of a customer by a CMS licence holder (licensee)?
o: Money received in respect of a sale of securities.
Money used to reduce the amount owed by the customer to the licensee.
Money used to defray the brokerage of the licensee.
Money paid to any person entitled to the money.
questions.e: In this context, the term money does not include money which is to be used to reduce the amount owed by the customer to the holder, money which is to be paid to the customer or in accordance with the customer's written direction, money which is to be used to defray the holder's brokerage and other proper charges, and money which is to be paid to any other person entitled to the money. Money received in respect of a sale of securities IS considered money.

questions.q: A Member or its representatives is prohibited from disclosing customer information to third parties unless:
o: The disclosure is required for effective execution of the customer's order.
Prior consent of the customer has been obtained.
The disclosure is necessary for increasing the possibility of profit in the trades being executed.
The disclosure is required to enhance the market standing of the Member.
questions.e: Information is not to be released to 3rd parties unless: it is with the prior consent of the customer, the disclosure is required for the effective execution of the customers' order, the disclosure is necessary for the operations and risk management of the intermediary and for the purpose of audit by internal and external auditors, lawyers, or consultants approved or engaged by the intermediary, and the disclosure is required under any law or rules for investigating or prosecuting an offence alleged or suspected to have been committed under any written law.

questions.q: BlueBird is a Trading Member (TM). BlueBird wants to appoint John as an APPOINTED Representative to deal in shares. John meets all the relevant entry and examination requirements to conduct the regulated activity of dealing in shares. Which of the following conditions must be satisfied before John is allowed to commence work as an APPOINTED Representative?
o: John must be notified by Blue Bird as an appointed representative under the FAA.
John's name must be entered into the Public Register of Representatives.
BlueBird must first register John as a Provisional Representative with SGX-ST.
BlueBird must give John 3 months training for dealing in shares.
questions.e: John must be notified as an appointed representative under the SFA (NOT the FAA). There is no requirement for BlueBird to give training to John.

questions.q: LMN corporation wants to apply for a CMSL for dealing in capital markets products, providing credit rating services, and providing custodial services. Jane is the CEO of LMN. LMN wants to appoint John, residing in Australia, as its director responsible for its Singapore business. In this context, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
o: LMN must employ at least 2 full time individuals in total to take care of the three regulated activities for which it is applying for licence.
LMN must obtain prior approval of the MAS before appointing any high level management personnel.
LMN must obtain prior approval of the MAS before appointing John as its director.
Jane must be a resident of Singapore.
questions.e: LMN must employ at least 2 full time individuals in respect of EACH regulated activity for which the corporation is seeking to be licenced to conduct. Therefore, it must employ 6 full time persons for the 3 regulated activities. LMN must obtain MAS' approval prior to appointing a person as its chief executive officer, its director who resides in Singapore or is to reside in Singapore, or its director who is directly responsible for its business in Singapore. The chief executive officer of LMN should also be a resident in Singapore. There is no need to obtain prior approval of the MAS before appointing ANY high level management personnel.

questions.q: General Licensing Criteria states that an applicant for CMS licence:
o: Should be primarily engaged in any one of the regulated activities.
Should have an established track record in the proposed activity in Singapore for at least 10 years.
Should have a good ranking in its home country.
Should be subject to proper supervision by its home regulatory authority.
questions.e: MAS would take into account whether the applicant is a reputable entity that has an established track record in the proposed activity to be conducted in Singapore or in a related field, for at least the past 5 years. The other statements are true.

questions.q: John buys shares on Monday (January 3). There are no market holidays until January 15. When should John's broker issue him the contract note for the transaction if the transaction needed to refer to the fixing price of 10th January?
o: 10 Jan
11 Jan
12 Jan
13 Jan
questions.e: Members must issue contract notes no later than the next business day following the transaction. However, if any detail about the transaction which needs to be included in the contract note is only available later, Members must issue the contract note by the next business day after the details are available. Therefore, the contract must be issued by 11 January.

questions.q: Trading Members are required to establish clear policies and procedures to comply with the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 and other confidentiality obligations in relation to their customers. This requires that their representatives should:
o: Check the DNC registry before making calls.
Seek clear and unambiguous consent via forms.
Seek clear and unambiguous consent verbally.
Ensure that the customers give their consent before the prescribed day.
questions.e: Members should establish clear policies and procedures to comply with the provisions of the PDPA and other confidentiality obligations such as requiring their representatives to check the DNC registry before making calls and seek clear and unambiguous consent (VIA Forms or call scripts). Violations of DNC policies and procedures will lead to disciplinary actions. Consent must be given before the prescribed day.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about deposit of money received from a customer by a CMS licence holder is FALSE?
o: The money should be deposited in a trust account or an account directed by the customer by the next business day after receipt.
Moneys received from different customers may be commingled and deposited in the same trust account.
Money received from a customer may be commingled with other funds.
None of the above.
questions.e: Money received from a customer may NOT be commingled with other funds. The other statements are true.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered as money received on account of a customer of a CMS licence holder?
o: Moneys received for maintenance of a securities trading account by a customer.
Moneys received when the licensee provides securities financing to the customer.
Moneys received for managing the funds of the customer.
Money which is to be paid to the customer.
questions.e: Money which is to be paid to the customer is NOT considered money. The other options state moneys which are considered received on account of a customer of a CMS licence holder.

questions.q: With which of the following entities/accounts can moneys received by a CMS licence holder on account of a customer be deposited?
o: With a clearing house for purposes specified in relevant rules.
In any account directed by the customer.
With a member of a securities exchange for purposes specified in the relevant rules.
All of the above.
questions.e: Moneys received by a CMS licence holder on account of a customer may be deposited with any of the given entities.

questions.q: If the outcome of a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) for a customer is positive, and the customer refuses to receive advice from the CMS licence holder, who is responsible for ensuring the suitability of the product selected for investment?
o: The CEO of the CMS licence holder.
The manager of the CMS licence holder.
The customer.
The representative of the CMS licence holder.
questions.e: Notwithstanding a positive outcome of the CKA, the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution should offer to provide advice concerning the unlisted SIP to the customer. If the customer does not wish to receive advice, the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution must document the customer's decision in writing and highlight to the customer that it is the customer's responsibility to ensure the suitability of the product selected.

questions.q: One of the criteria for being granted a CMS licence is that the board of directors of the applicant should comprise of a minimum of ____.
o: 6 members
8 members
3 members
2 members
questions.e: One of the criteria for being granted a CMS licence is that the board of directors of the applicant should comprise of a minimum of 2 members.

questions.q: LMN is a Trading Member and wants to appoint John as his Trading Representative. Which of the following due diligence checks must LMN perform on John to ascertain his fitness and propriety?
o: Reference checks with the previous employer to find out if John was dismissed or asked to resign.
Checking public records to find out if John has a criminal record.
Checking records from the Ministry of Law's Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office Online Portal to ensure that John is not an undischarged bankrupt in Singapore.
Checking John's social media account to understand his political views.
questions.e: Professional track record, financial status and criminal records must be checked. Social media accounts need not be checked.

questions.q: Provisional representatives are allowed a grace period of ____ to pass the requisite examinations applicable to appointed representatives.
o: 6 months
3 months
12 months
1 month
questions.e: Provisional representatives are given a grace period of three months to complete the requisite examinations applicable to appointed representatives.

questions.q: LMN is a Trading Member (TM). LMN wants to appoint John as a PROVISIONAL Representative to deal in shares. Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for John's appointment as a PROVISIONAL Representative?
o: John must possess the same educational qualifications as required for appointed representatives.
John must have passed the relevant exams, as required by appointed representatives.
John must be working for a related entity of LMN.
John must be currently licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated for the regulated activity in any overseas jurisdiction.
questions.e: Provisional representatives are given a grace period of three months to complete the requisite examinations applicable to appointed representatives. During the grace period, they are allowed to conduct regulated activities. In addition to educational and work experience-related admission criteria (including 3 years of relevant work experience), provisional representatives must be CURRENTLY OR PREVIOUSLY licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated for a continuous period of at least 12 months (and not more than 12 months before) for the relevant activity in an overseas jurisdiction with a regulatory regime that is COMPARABLE (NOT ANY JURISDICTION) to that of Singapore.

questions.q: JKL corporation is a restricted broker dealing in securities. JKL:
o: May deal in securities with accredited investors.
May deal in securities with expert investors.
May accept assets from any customer as a margin for any sale of securities by that customer.
May carry customer's positions in its own books.
questions.e: Refers to a corporation which deals in securities, units in a collective investment scheme or exchange-traded derivatives contracts which (i) does not carry any customer's positions in those capital markets products, margins or accounts in its own books; (ii) deals in those capital markets products only with accredited investors, expert investors or institutional investors; (iii) does not accept money or assets from any customer as settlement of, or as a margin for, or to guarantee or secure, any contract for the purchase or sale of those capital markets products by that customer; and (iv) does not enter into any transaction with any customer to deal in those capital markets products as principal.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about providing advice concerning an SIP to a customer is TRUE?
o: If the outcome of CAR is positive, advice should not be provided.
If the outcome of CKA is positive, advice should not be provided.
If the outcome of CKA is positive, and the customer refuses to receive advice, the CMSL holder should not trade in the SIP on behalf of the customer.
If the outcome of CAR is positive, the customer may request for advice.
questions.e: Regardless of the outcome of the CAR, a CMSL holder or an exempt financial institution must include a statement in its account opening form that a customer can, at any time, request for advice concerning a SIP. If requested, advice must be provided. Even if the outcome of the CKA is positive, the CMSL holders or exempt financial institutions should offer to provide advice on the unlisted SIP to the customer. If the customer does not wish to receive advice, the customer's decision must be documented in writing. The customer should be told in writing that it is his responsibility to ensure the suitability of the product selected. The customer should be warned in writing that he has chosen not to receive advice and decided to proceed without advice.

questions.q: In the case of a CMS licensee, the base capital can be calculated by which of the following formulas?
o: Paid-up ordinary share capital + Paid-up irredeemable and non-cumulative preference share capital - Reserve fund + Unappropriated profit or loss - Interim loss -dividend declared since the latest audited accounts.

Paid-up ordinary share capital + Paid-up irredeemable and non-cumulative preference share capital + Reserve fund + Unappropriated profit or loss - Interim loss -dividend declared since the latest audited accounts.

Paid-up ordinary share capital + Paid-up irredeemable and non-cumulative preference share capital + Reserve fund - Unappropriated profit or loss + Interim loss -dividend declared since the latest audited accounts.

Paid-up ordinary share capital - Paid-up irredeemable and non-cumulative preference share capital + Reserve fund + Unappropriated profit or loss + Interim loss -dividend declared since the latest audited accounts.
questions.e: Regulations) Base capital = Paid-up ordinary share capital + Paid-up irredeemable and non-cumulative preference share capital + Reserve fund + Unappropriated profit or loss - Interim loss -dividend declared since the latest audited accounts.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder for dealing in securities which is a foreign company, and which is a member of an approved clearing house must maintain a reserve fund if its net head office funds fall below the prescribed minimum. What is the minimum amount that must be transferred annually to the reserve in such a situation?
o: Minimum 30% of the audited net profits after providing for taxation.
Minimum 40% of the audited net profits after providing for taxation.
Minimum 50% of the audited net profits after providing for taxation.
Minimum 10% of the audited net profits before providing for taxation.
questions.e: Regulations) Minimum 30% of the audited net profits after providing for taxation must be transferred annually to the reserve in such a situation.

questions.q: A Contract Note is required to contain which of the following information:
o: The amount of the consideration for the transaction
Any amounts that are to be added or deducted from the transaction.
Source of funds of the customer.
The amount of stamp duty payable for the transaction.
questions.e: Source of funds of the customer NEED NOT be included in the contract note. The information given in the other options must be included.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Specified Investment Products (SIPs) is/are TRUE?
o: SIPs may be listed on the exchange.
SIPs have complex features and risks.
SIPs are usually riskier than equities.
SIPs are derivatives or products that may contain derivatives.
questions.e: Specified Investment Products (SIPs) are derivatives or products which may contain derivatives. They have complex features and risks which can expose investors to more factors which can cause a loss. Some SIPs are listed on an exchange while others are not. SIPs are derivatives, or products that contain derivatives.

questions.q: A temporary representative may be appointed for a total of 6 months within any ____ period, with each appointment not lasting more than ____.
o: 36 months, 3 months
12 months, 3 months
24 months, 3 months
24 months, 6 months
questions.e: Temporary representatives are appointed to conduct regulated activities on a short-term basis. They are eligible to be appointed for a total of 6 months within any 24-month period, with each appointment not lasting more than 3 months.

questions.q: Within how many months after the end of the financial year a CMS licence holder must submit its profit and loss accounts and balance sheet to MAS?
o: 2 months.
3 months.
5 months.
6 months.
questions.e: The account and balance sheet must be lodged with MAS by the CMS licence holder within 5 months after the end of the financial year, together with the auditor's report on the account and balance sheet.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the audit of accounts of a CMSL holder is/are TRUE?
o: The account, balance sheet, and the auditor's report must be lodged with MAS within 3 months after the end of the financial year.
If requested by the CMSL holder, the MAS may extend the last date of submission of accounts, balance sheet and auditor's report by up to 4 months.
The MAS may directly remove the auditor of a CMSL holder if it is not satisfied with the auditor's performance.
The auditor should submit the account, balance sheet and auditor's report to the MAS directly in all cases.
questions.e: The account, balance sheet, and auditor's report must be lodged by the CMSL holder with MAS within 5 months after the end of the financial year. The auditor must immediately send a report in writing directly to MAS IF it discovers certain specified irregularities or issues. The CMS licence holder may apply to MAS for an extension of the 5-month period. If MAS is satisfied that there is a special reason for requiring an extension, it will extend the period by not more than 4 months. MAS may direct a CMS licence holder to remove and replace its auditor if it is not satisfied with the performance of duties by the auditor. MAS cannot remove the auditor directly.

questions.q: In relation to depositing money in a trust account held with a financial institution, a CMS Licence holder (licensee) is required to obtain an acknowledgement from the financial institution. What should the acknowledgement include?
o: That the moneys are held on trust by the licensee for its customer.
That the financial institution cannot exercise any set-off right against the moneys owed by the licensee to the institution.
That the account shall be maintained separately from any other account where the licensee deposits its money.
All of the above.
questions.e: The acknowledgement should include all the given terms.

questions.q: The regulations relating to publishing of advertisements by CMS licensees and representatives require that the advertisements:
o: Must contain only information that the advertiser knows or believes to be true.
Can make guarantees related to assured profits subject to monetary limits.
Cannot claim that the advertiser's abilities have been approved by the Authority.
Can claim that the advertiser's qualifications have been approved by the Authority.
questions.e: The advertisement must contain only information that the advertiser knows or believes to be true, and it should not misrepresent the authorisation, licence or permission, if any, which they possess from the regulating bodies (such as MAS and SGX). The advertisement cannot make guarantees related to assured profits or claim that the advertiser's qualifications have been approved by the Authority.

questions.q: The applicant for a CMS licence must employ minimum how many full-time individuals in respect of each regulated activity?
o: Two.
Three.
Four.
Seven.
questions.e: The applicant is required to employ at least 2 full time individuals in respect of each regulated activity for which the corporation is seeking to be licenced to conduct.

questions.q: The applicant for grant of CMS licence is required to employ a minimum of how many full time individuals in respect of each regulated activity for which it is requesting for a licence?
questions.e: The applicant is required to employ at least 2 full time individuals in respect of each regulated activity for which the corporation is seeking to be licenced. These individuals must be appointed as representatives for the relevant regulated activity as required under the SFA.

questions.q: Which of the following requirements is/are included in the general criteria for grant of a CMS licence?
o: The applicant must be primarily engaged in the business of conducting any one of the regulated activities.
The applicant must be operating out of a physical office in Singapore.
The applicant must have reported a net profit in at least 3 out of the previous 6 years.
The applicant must satisfy that it will discharge its duties efficiently, honestly and fairly.
questions.e: The applicant should be primarily engaged in the business of conducting any one of the regulated activities and be operating out of a physical office in Singapore. The applicant must satisfy that it will discharge its duties efficiently, honestly and fairly. Net profit is NOT a criteria for the grant of a CMS licence. However, financial soundness is considered from the point of view of fitness and propriety.

questions.q: Under Section 47 of the Banking Act, a bank in Singapore or any of its officers cannot disclose customer information to any third party except as permitted under the Banking Act. The situations where such a disclosure is permitted include where the disclosure is:
o: based on the prior written consent of the customer.
necessary for risk management of the bank.
necessary for the internal audit by internal and external auditors engaged by the bank.
in the interests of the customer, as determined by the appointed representative.
questions.e: The Banking Act does not grant any authority to appointed representatives to disclose customer information to any third party based on their discretion.

questions.q: Jane wants to open an SIP trading account for UNLISTED SIPs with BigBoy (a CMSL holder). She fails the CKA assessment and is deemed not to possess the required knowledge or experience in derivatives. In this context, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
o: BigBoy must inform Jane that it failed the CKA assessment.
BigBoy cannot transact in SIPs on behalf of Jane.
BigBoy shall provide Financial Advisory services to Jane according to standards in the Notice on Recommendations on Investment Products.
BigBoy must obtain an indemnity bond from Jane before allowing her to transact in unlisted SIPs.
questions.e: The BigBoy (a CMSL holder) MUST inform Jane of the outcome of the CKA. If Jane still intends to proceed to open a SIP trading, BigBoy may proceed to transact in the unlisted SIP on behalf of the customer. This is because BigBoy (a CMSL holder) is an Exempt Financial Advisor (FA). Since BigBoy is an exempt FA, it shall provide financial advisory services to the customer in accordance with the standards set out in the Notice on Recommendations on Investment Products. Note that if BigBoy were not an exempt FA, it would not have been allowed to proceed to transact in unlisted SIPs on Jane's behalf.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder is required to keep books of accounts under the SFA. Such books are required to be retained for a period of ____.
o: not less than 3 years
not less than 5 years
not less than 10 years
not less than 7 years
questions.e: The books should be kept for a period of at least 5 years, and in a manner which would enable them to be conveniently and properly audited.

questions.q: If a CMS licence holder is unable to lodge its financial statements with the MAS within the prescribed time after completion of the financial year, it may apply to the MAS for an extension of the deadline for submission. The MAS may grant an extension of up to ____.
o: 14 days
30 days
3 months
4 months
questions.e: The CMS licence holder may apply to the MAS for an extension of the 5-month period for lodgement of account and balance sheet. If MAS is satisfied that there is a special reason for requiring an extension, it will extend the period by not more than 4 months, subject to conditions or restrictions which MAS may think fit to impose.

questions.q: Can a CMS licence holder (licensee) maintain a custody account for depositing the assets of a customer with itself?
o: Yes, all licensees are allowed.
No, to avoid conflict of interest, no licensee can do so.
Licensees can do so provided they are allowed under the relevant Act to provide custodial services.
None of the above.
questions.e: The CMS licence holder may maintain the custody account itself where it is licensed under the Act to provide custodial services.

questions.q:
Olivia, a senior advisor at Trust Financial Services ('Trust'), recently conducted a Customer Account Review (CAR) for her client, Nathan, who is interested in trading listed Specified Investment Products (SIPs). The CAR was conducted two years and eleven months ago, and Nathan has been actively trading listed SIPs through his account. Nathan now wishes to explore new listed SIPs. Olivia reviews Nathan's trading activity and notes that he has transacted in listed SIPs more than once during the preceding three-year period.

According to the guidelines for the validity of the outcome of CAR, what should Olivia do next before allowing Nathan to transact in new listed SIPs?
o: Olivia should immediately allow Nathan to transact in new listed SIPs without any further action, as his active trading history indicates sufficient experience.
Olivia should conduct a new CAR for Nathan, as the validity of the previous CAR is about to expire and it is a requirement for trading in new listed SIPs.
Olivia should check if Nathan intends to actively transact in listed SIPs in the near future before allowing him to transact in new listed SIPs.
Olivia should inform Nathan that he needs to wait until the three-year mark has passed from the date of the last CAR before conducting any new transactions in listed SIPs.
questions.e: The CMS licence holder must not allow a customer to transact in a listed SIP through the listed SIP trading account after 3 years has expired from the date of the conduct of the CAR for the customer concerned, UNTIL AND UNLESS: i. The CMS licence holder has checked and is satisfied that the customer has transacted in a listed SIP through the account a) More than once during the preceding 3-year period; and b) More than once during each subsequent 3-year period; OR ii. The CMS licence holder has conducted a new CAR for the customer or has relied on a new CAR conducted by a third party for the customer. In the given case, Nathan has transacted more than once in the relevant products during the 3 year period. Therefore, (A) is correct as there is no need to conduct another CAR.

questions.q: For how long should an exempt financial institution keep a customer's acknowledgement of the risk warning statement for trading in overseas-listed investment products?
o: Minimum 2 years
Minimum 1 year
Minimum 5 years
Minimum 10 years
questions.e: The CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution must maintain records of the Customer's acknowledgement for a period of not less than 5 years as per the SFA 102(3) Keeping of Book and Furnishing of Returns.

questions.q: Validity of the positive outcome of a Customer Account Review (CAR) must be reviewed after ____.
o: 1 year
two years
three years
four years
questions.e: The CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution must not allow a customer to transact in an SIP through the SIP trading account after 3 years have expired from the date of the conduct of the CAR for the customer concerned, unless certain conditions are fulfilled.

questions.q: With which of the following entities can a CMS licence holder maintain a custody account for depositing the assets of a customer?
o: A merchant bank licensed under the Banking Act
A finance company licensed under the Finance Companies Act.
A depository agent within the meaning of the relevant section of the Companies Act for specified securities.
All of the above.
questions.e: The CMS licensee may maintain a custody account for depositing the assets of a customer with any of the given entities .

questions.q: Which of the following information must be included in contract notes for sale or purchase of securities?
o: A statement that the CMS licence holder is acting as a principal, if it is dealing in securities as a principal.
Name under which the CMS licence holder carries on business of dealing in securities.
Reasons for carrying out the trade.
Relevant stamp duties
questions.e: The contract note should, inter-alia, contain the name under which the CMS licence holder carries on its business of dealing in securities, and the address of the principal place of business, a statement informing the customer that the CMS licence holder is dealing in securities as a principal if the CMS licence holder is doing so, and the amount of all stamp duties or other duties or taxes payable. Reasons for carrying out the trade is NOT included in the contract note.

questions.q: If the CMS Licence holder (licensee) maintains a custody account with a custodian for the assets of a customer, the custodian can claim a right of retention over any asset under certain circumstances. Which of the following situations are included in those circumstances?
o: Where the customer is likely to default.
Where the licensee has obtained written permission from the customer.
Where the custodian has obtained written permission from the customer.
Where the terms and conditions provide such retention in respect of any charges related to custody of the asset.
questions.e: The custodian shall not claim any lien, right of retention or sale over any asset standing to the credit of the custody account, EXCEPT where the holder has obtained the customer's written consent and notified the custodian in writing of the written consent, or in respect of any charges as agreed upon in the terms and conditions relating to the administration or custody of the asset.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about customer's money with a CMSL holder is TRUE?
o: The financial institution with which customer's money is deposited may exercise a right of set-off against the money for any debt owed by the CMSL holder to the financial institution.
A CMSL holder (dealing in securities) cannot deposit money received on account of its customer with a clearing house.
Interest earned from the maintenance of the money received on account of the customer in a trust account accrue to the CMSL holder.
A Trading Member must notify the remisier of any withdrawal of remisier's money made from a trust account by the next business day
questions.e: The financial institution CANNOT set off the money against any debt owed by the CMSL holder to the financial institution. A CMSL holder (dealing in securities) MAY deposit moneys received on account of its customer with a clearing house. Interest earned from the maintenance of the moneys received on account of the customer in a trust account accrue to the CUSTOMER.

questions.q: What is the minimum Base Capital Requirement for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is a non-clearing member?
o: SGD 5 million
SGD 1 million
SGD 3 million
questions.e: The minimum Base Capital Requirement for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is a non-clearing member is SGD 1 million.

questions.q: What is the minimum Base Capital Requirement to be satisfied for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is a non-member?
o: SGD 1 million
SGD 2 million
SGD 3 million
SGD 10 million
questions.e: The minimum Base Capital Requirement to be satisfied for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is a non-member is SGD 1 million.

questions.q: What is the minimum Base Capital Requirement to be satisfied for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is an introducing broker?
o: SGD 2 million
SGD 1 million
SGD 5 million
questions.e: The minimum Base Capital Requirement to be satisfied for dealing in securities by a CMS licence holder who is an introducing broker is SGD 500,000.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder must satisfy the minimum Base Capital Requirement (BCR) for its proposed regulated activities. What is the minimum BCR for dealing in securities by a clearing member?
o: SGD 1 million
SGD 2 million
SGD 5 million
questions.e: The minimum BCR for dealing in securities by a clearing member is SGD 5 million.

questions.q: Broadly, the minimum licensing admission criteria for a corporation for Capital Markets Services Licence is that:
o: It should be financially sound.
It should be reputable.
It should be prudently managed.
It should have been operating successfully in Singapore for at least 20 years.
questions.e: The minimum licensing admission criteria for corporations applying for a CMS licence ensure that only financially sound and reputable corporations that are prudently managed and directed by officers who are competent and have integrity, are granted a CMS licence. There is no requirement to have a track record of 20 years in Singapore.

questions.q: Which of the following information should be included in contract notes for sale or purchase of securities?
o: The amount of the consideration for the transaction
Any amounts that are to be added or deducted from the transaction
The price per unit of the transaction
The overall margin account balance of the customer.
questions.e: The overall margin account balance of the customer need not be included in the contract note.

questions.q: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) DOES NOT apply to personal data related to an individual that is contained in a record that has been in existence for minimum ____.
o: 100 years
7 years
10 years
5 years
questions.e: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) DOES NOT apply to personal data related to an individual that is contained in a record that has been in existence for minimum 100 years.

questions.q: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) provisions regarding disclosure of personal data apply in relation to a deceased person who has been dead for ____.
o: minimum 5 years
maximum 10 years
minimum 15 years
maximum 20 years
questions.e: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) provisions regarding disclosure of personal data apply in relation to a deceased person who has been dead for maximum 10 years.

questions.q: In the case of overseas-listed investment products, the CMS licence holder is required to provide a risk warning statement to its customers. The risk warning statement must highlight which of the following risks?
o: Level of investor protection and safeguards provided in the foreign jurisdiction.
Differences between the legal systems prevalent in the foreign jurisdiction and in Singapore.
Currency risks.
Maximum possible returns that can be made from investing in the products.
questions.e: The risk warning statement highlights the key risks that customers should be aware of when trading overseas-listed investment products, such as the level of investor protection and safeguards afforded in the relevant foreign jurisdiction, the differences between the legal systems in foreign jurisdiction and Singapore, tax implications, currency risks, and additional transaction costs that may be incurred, exposure to counterparty and correspondent broker risks, and political, economic and social developments that may influence overseas markets. Maximum possible return from investment is NOT included.

questions.q: The decision of the MAS on whether to revoke the status of an individual as an appointed representative depends on which of the following factors?
o: The severity of circumstances in which the person failed to meet the required criteria.
The relevance of the unfulfilled criteria in relation to the duties of the representative.
The time elapsed since the person failed to meet the criteria.
The social status of the person when he failed to meet the criteria.
questions.e: The social status of the person when he failed to meet the criteria is irrelevant in this context. The factors mentioned in the other three options will be considered by the MAS to decide whether to revoke the registration of a CMS licensee in this context.

questions.q: The status of a provisional representative is only valid for a maximum of 3 months. The 3-month period is calculated from which date?
o: The date his name is entered into the Public Register of Representatives.
The date he joins office.
The date he is allowed to independently provide advice to clients.
The date he is appointed by his principal.
questions.e: The status of a provisional representative is only valid for a maximum of 3 months from the date his name is entered into the Public Register of Representatives.

questions.q: In which of the following circumstances will the status of an appointed representative in respect of any regulated activity cease to be valid?
o: If MAS revokes the licence of the principal.
After one year from the date of registration.
If the principal stops carrying on business in the particular type of regulated activity.
If the licence of his principal lapses for a regulated activity that is different from that for which the representative is appointed.
questions.e: The status of an appointed, provisional or temporary representative in respect of any regulated activity is valid until it ceases, inter-alia, if the MAS revokes the licence of the principal or the principal ceases to carry on business in THAT TYPE of regulated activity.

questions.q: In the context of money received by a CMS licence holder (licensee) on account of a customer, which of the following statements is FALSE?
o: The licensee must deal with the money as belonging to that customer.
The term money excludes money received on account of the customer in the course of the business of the licensee.
The term money excludes money used to defray the proper charges of the licensee.
None of the above.
questions.e: The term money INCLUDES money received on account of the customer in the course of the business of the licensee. The other statements are true.

questions.q: The terms and conditions regarding provision of custodial services for securities by a CMS licence holder (licensee) CANNOT include:
o: Conditions related to any lien over the assets by a third party.
The circumstances when the licensee may sell personal assets of the customer to recover sums due to it.
The liability of the customer in the event of default of the custodian.
Conditions related to any security interest in the asset by the licensee.
questions.e: The terms CANNOT include the circumstances when the licensee may sell PERSONAL assets of the customer to recover sums due to it, or the liability of the CUSTOMER in the event of default of the custodian. Conditions related to any lien over the assets by a third party and security interest in the asset by the licensee are included.

questions.q: For being eligible for registration as a Trading Representative, an applicant must be at least how many years old?
o: 18 years.
21 years.
24 years.
30 years.
questions.e: To be appointed as a trading representative, the applicant must be minimum 21 years old, possess the minimum education level (e.g., equivalent to at least 4 GCE O-Level credit passes), pass the relevant exams and be fit and proper.

questions.q: Based on the minimum educational requirements for being appointed as a trading representative, which of the following applicants may definitely be considered eligible?
o: An applicant with 4 GCE-O Level credit passes who has no work experience.
An applicant with 2 GCE-O Level credit passes, if he has 3 continuous years of relevant working experience over the last 10 years.
An applicant with 5 years work experience over the last 10 years.
All of the above.
questions.e: To be appointed as a trading representative, the applicant must be minimum 21 years old, possess the minimum education level (e.g., equivalent to at least 4 GCE O-Level credit passes), pass the relevant exams and be fit and proper.

questions.q: Trading members are required to ensure that data and records are kept for a minimum period of ____.
o: 2 years.
7 years.
5 years.
10 years.
questions.e: Trading members are required to ensure that data and records are kept for a minimum period of 5 years.

questions.q: Trading Members are required to keep particulars of every proprietary transaction, including ____.
o: The price and fee arising from the transaction.
The realised or unrealised gain or loss.
The name of the counterparty to the transaction.
All of the above.
questions.e: Trading Members are required to keep all the given particulars of every proprietary transaction.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about maintenance of Trust and custody accounts of customers by Members is/are FALSE?
o: The account cannot be maintained with a Finance Company licensed under the Finance Companies Act.
A trust account for depositing customers' moneys in foreign currencies may be maintained outside Singapore with the written consent of the customer.
Custody accounts can be maintained with any person licensed under the SFA to provide custodial services for securities.
Custody accounts can be maintained with an approved trustee for a collective investment scheme.
questions.e: Trust and custody accounts CAN be maintained with a FINANCE company licensed under the Finance Companies Act (Cap. 108). The other statements are true.

questions.q: Under the PDPA, if an appeal is made, the Chairman of the Appeal Panel is to nominate ____ or more members of the Appeal Panel to constitute an Appeal Committee to hear the appeal.
o: Three.
Four.
Ten.
Seventeen.
questions.e: Under the PDPA, if an appeal is made, the Chairman of the Appeal Panel is to nominate 3 or more members of the Appeal Panel to constitute an Appeal Committee to hear the appeal.

questions.q: Under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), which of the following CANNOT be considered personal data?
o: True data about an individual who can be identified from that data.
False data about an individual who can be identified from that data.
False data about an individual who cannot be identified from that data and other information available with the organisation.
All of the above.
questions.e: Under the PDPA, personal data means data, whether true or not, about an individual who CAN be identified from that data, or from that data and other information to which the organisation has or is likely to have access.

questions.q: Which of the following operations is/are covered under the term Processing of personal data in the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)?
o: Holding.
Combination.
Transmission.
Erasure.
questions.e: Under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), the term processing in relation to personal data, means the carrying out of any operation or set of operations in relation to the personal data, and includes recording, holding, organisation, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, combination, transmission, or erasure or destruction of data.

questions.q: Under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), the term Processing of personal data includes which of the following operations?
o: Recording.
Organisation.
Adaptation.
All of the above.
questions.e: Under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), the term processing in relation to personal data, means the carrying out of any operation or set of operations in relation to the personal data, and includes recording, holding, organisation, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, combination, transmission, or erasure or destruction of data.

questions.q: A CMS licence holder is required to send a contract note to its customer for a transaction in shares ____.
o: by the next working day
within two working days
within 3 market days
by the next business day following the transaction
questions.e: Under the SFR (LCB), a CMS licence holder must send its customer a contract note for the purchase or sale of securities or futures contracts by the next business day following a transaction.

questions.q: If an exempt financial institution does not implement a system to identify and determine whether an overseas-listed investment product is an excluded investment product (EIP):
o: The exempt FI should not sell the overseas-listed investment product.
The exempt FI should sell the overseas-listed investment product only to accredited investors.
The overseas-listed investment product must be classified as an EIP.
The requirements to conduct the CAR shall apply to an exempt financial institution dealing in the overseas-listed investment product for a customer.
questions.e: Where a CMS licence holder or an exempt financial institution does not implement a system to identify and determine that an overseas-listed investment product is to be classified as an excluded investment product, the overseas-listed investment product shall be classified as a specified investment product, and the requirements to conduct the CAR shall apply to a CMS licence holder or an exempt financial institution dealing in the overseas-listed investment product for a customer.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the classification of an overseas-listed investment product as an excluded investment product (EIP) by a CMSL holder is/are TRUE?
o: If an overseas-listed investment product is classified as an EIP, it shall remain an EIP for 1 year.
The CMSL holder must ensure that the classification of the overseas-listed investment product remains accurate and current at all times.
A CMSL holder must treat all overseas-listed investment products as EIPs till they are classified as SIP.
A CMS licence holder may outsource the identification and classification of an overseas-listed investment product as an EIP to another party.
questions.e: Where a CMS licence holder or an exempt financial institution has classified an overseas-listed investment product as an excluded investment product, it shall ensure the classification remains accurate and current at all times. A CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution may outsource the identification and classification of an overseas-listed investment product as an excluded investment product to another party, but the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution shall be responsible for the implementation of the classification system, including the accuracy of the classification.

questions.q: In the context of allowing a customer to trade in unlisted Specified Investment Products, the validity of a Customer Knowledge Assessment is ____.
o: One year.
Two years.
Three years.
6 months.
questions.e: Where a customer is assessed to have knowledge or experience to transact in an unlisted SIP, the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution may allow the customer to transact the unlisted SIP for a period of one year from the date of the assessment.

questions.q: A CMS Licence will lapse:
o: if a CMS licence holder is wound up or dissolved whether in Singapore or elsewhere.
if a CMS licence holder changes its directors.
if there is a change in shareholders of a CMS licence holder.
if a Trading Representative of a CMS licence holder loses his/her licence.
questions.e: A CMS Licence will lapse if a CMS licence holder is wound up or dissolved whether in Singapore or elsewhere. The licence will not lapse if there is a change in the directors or the shareholders of the licensee, or if a representative of the Member loses his licence.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about segregation of customer's monies and assets and fiduciary obligations are TRUE?
o: A Member is required to deposit customers' monies and assets in trust or custody accounts.
A Member may commingle moneys from different customers in the same trust account.
A member may not deposit his own monies into the trust account even for the purpose of maintaining the account.
A Member must separately account for monies and assets of each customer.
questions.e: A Member shall segregate customers' moneys and assets from the Member's monies and assets, and deposit customers' moneys and assets in trust or custody accounts. A Member may commingle moneys from different customers into the same trust account, but must separately account for the monies and assets of each customer. A Member MAY deposit its own monies into the trust account for the purpose of maintaining the account.

questions.q: A Capital Markets Services licence can be granted to ____.
o: A natural person.
A Singapore corporation.
A natural person or a corporation.
A foreign corporation which does not have any office in Singapore.
questions.e: CMS licence holders are licensed and regulated under the SFA. A corporation may make an application for a CMS licence to carry on business in one or more of the regulated activities as specified in the SFA.

questions.q: If any representative of a CMS licence holder fails to meet the 'Fit and Proper' criteria, it is required to report the matter within ____.
o: 14 days.
7 days.
21 days.
30 days.
questions.e: CMS licence holders must also ensure that independent and rigorous due diligence checks are conducted to ensure that representatives meet the Fit and Proper criteria. They have to file a Report on Misconduct of Representative if any of its representatives fail to meet the Fit and Proper criteria or have committed acts relating to market misconduct within 14 days after the discovery of the misconduct.

questions.q: John receives monthly statements from his stock broker for the transactions executed in January and March. The broker does not send the January to March quarterly statement to John. His broker:
o: is guilty of an offence under SFR(LCB).
need not send the quarterly statement to John.
may send a quarterly statement to John in addition to the two monthly statements.
must send the February statement to John even if there were no transactions in that month.
questions.e: If a monthly statement has not been sent for the last month of a calendar quarter (i.e., March, June, September and December), the Member shall send a quarterly statement to the customer, containing the same required information. Else, the quarterly statement need not be sent. The monthly statement for February need not be sent if there has been no change to the customer's account in the month.

questions.q: In case all the relevant information is available, a contract note is required to be issued by the Trading Member no later than ____.
o: The next business day following the transaction.
The next calendar day after the transaction.
The close of business on the same day on which the transaction was executed.
The third business day after the transaction.
questions.e: Members shall issue contract notes no later than the next business day following the transaction. If any detail about the transaction which needs to be included in the contract note is only available later, Members shall issue the contract note by the next business day after the details are available.

questions.q: According to the General Licensing Criteria for grant of CMS licence, which of the following persons relating to the applicant's organisation are required to be 'Fit and Proper' as per the MAS guidelines?
o: Its employees.
Its representatives.
Its substantial shareholders.
All of the above.
questions.e: The applicant, its officers, employees, representatives and substantial shareholders must be fit and proper persons in accordance with MAS' Guidelines on Fit and Proper Criteria.

questions.q: The board of directors of the applicant for grant of CMS licence should have minimum how many members?
questions.e: The board of directors should comprise a minimum of 2 members, at least one of whom is resident in Singapore

questions.q: Which of the following are the duties of a CMSL holder?
o: To participate in official discussions on appropriate code of conduct and governance practices.
To ensure effective control and segregation procedures to mitigate potential conflict of interest.
To identify, address and monitor risks associated with its trading and business activities.
To submit post-mortem reports to MAS on issues highlighted by auditors.
questions.e: A CMSL holder must ensure effective control and segregation procedures to mitigate potential conflicts of interest. It must identify, address and monitor risks associated with its trading and business activities. Participating in official discussions on appropriate code of conduct and governance practices and submitting post-mortem reports to MAS on issues highlighted by auditors are not the duties of CMSL holders.

questions.q: John is an appointed representative for PQR Limited (a CMSL holder). John can apply to the MAS to simultaneously act as an appointed representative for which of the following entities? Presume that the other entity is also a CMSL holder for the same regulated activity.
o: PQR's subsidiary.
PQR's holding company.
PQR's substantial shareholder company.
A company that is a subsidiary of PQR's holding company.
questions.e: A representative can act for only one principal unless it has the approval of MAS to act for more than one principal, or if the principals are related corporations. Corporations are considered related corporations if one is the subsidiary or holding company (>50% voting shares) of another, or both are subsidiaries of the same corporation (fellow subsidiaries). Substantial shareholding means holding >5% voting shares.

questions.q: LMN corporation wants to apply for a CMSL for dealing in capital markets products. PQR Corporation is LMN's holding company. Which of the following persons/entities must be "fit and proper" for LMN to be considered for grant of the licence?
o: LMN Corporation
PQR Corporation
Vendors that supply and maintain critical IT infrastructure for LMN
LMN's employees
questions.e: The applicant for a CMSL, its officers, employees, representatives and substantial shareholders must be "fit and proper" persons in accordance with MAS Guidelines on Fit and Proper Criteria (FSG-G01). A holding company (>50% voting power) is a substantial shareholder (holding >5% voting shares).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Specified Investment products (SIP) and SIP trading accounts for retail customers is/are FALSE?
o: They may or may not contain derivatives.
Customer Account Review is not required to be conducted for SIPs listed on an exchange.
Equity-linked structured notes are listed on an exchange.
All of the above.
questions.e: Specified Investment Products (SIPs) are derivatives or products which may contain derivatives (a derivative is always involved). CKA is required for unlisted SIPs and CAR is required for listed SIPs (before opening the trading account for a retail customer). SIPs have complex features and risks which can expose investors to more factors which can cause a loss. Equity-linked structured notes are NOT listed on exchanges.

questions.q: An exempt financial institution must not allow a customer to transact in a Specified Investment Product (SIP) through the SIP trading account after 3 years have elapsed from the date of conduct of the CAR unless:
o: It is satisfied that the customer has transacted in a listed SIP through the account more than once during the past 2 years.
A new Customer Account Review has been conducted.
The customer is a retail investor.
The customer has at least $500,000 in his bank account.
questions.e: The CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution must not allow a customer to transact in a SIP through the SIP trading account after 3 years have expired from the date of the conduct of the CAR for the customer concerned, until and unless: the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution has checked and is satisfied that the customer has transacted in a listed SIP through the account more than once during the preceding 3-year period, and more than once during each subsequent 3-year period, OR the CMS licence holder or exempt financial institution has conducted a new CAR for the customer.

questions.q:
Caroline, a client service manager at Atlas Investment Solutions ('Atlas'), is reviewing the monthly statements sent to clients to ensure they meet the regulatory requirements outlined in the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations. She notices that for several clients, the statements do not include detailed information on the clients' transactions in securities or units in a collective investment scheme and the prices at which the transactions were entered into. Additionally, the statements lack a detailed account of all financial charges and credits to the clients' accounts during the statement period.

According to the guidelines for the provision of monthly statements to customers, which of the following elements must Caroline ensure are included in the monthly statements to comply with regulatory requirements?
o: The clients' transactions in securities or units in a collective investment scheme and the prices at which the transactions are entered into.
The clients' outstanding positions in derivatives contracts and spot foreign exchange contracts.
The status of every asset of the client that Atlas is holding in custody.
A detailed account of all financial charges and credits to the clients' accounts during the statement period.
questions.e: (A) and (D) are correct because the guidelines stipulate that monthly statements must contain detailed information on the clients' transactions in securities or units in a collective investment scheme and the prices at which the transactions were entered into, as well as a detailed account of all financial charges and credits to the clients' accounts during the statement period. (B) and (C) are also important elements but were not the focus of the discrepancy Caroline noticed.

questions.q: An individual may be considered an accredited investor if his net personal assets exceed ____.
o: $1 million
$2 million
questions.e: Accredited Investor includes an individual whose net personal assets exceed in value $2 million, or whose income in the preceding 12 months is not less than $300,000.

questions.q: A corporation may be considered an accredited investor if its net assets exceed ____.
o: $30 million in value
$20 million in value
$10 million in value
$50 million in value
questions.e: An Accredited Investor includes a corporation with NET assets exceeding $10 million in value.

questions.q: In which of the following cases will an individual be considered an accredited investor? If his income in the preceding 12 months is ____.
questions.e: An Accredited Investor includes an individual whose net personal assets exceed $2 million, or whose income in the preceding 12 months is not less than $300,000. Therefore, a person with an income of S$305,000 (>S$300,000) will be considered an accredited investor.

questions.q: Which of the following entities is/are included in the definition of an Institutional Investor under the SFA?
o: All cooperative societies in Singapore.
A statutory board.
A pension fund.
A CMS licence holder for providing custodial services for securities.
questions.e: An Institutional Investor refers to a bank, a merchant bank, a finance company, a company/co-operative society LICENSED AS an INSURER in Singapore, a Trust company, the Government, a statutory board, a pension fund/collective investment scheme, a CMS licence holder for securities dealing, fund management, providing custodial services for securities, REIT management, securities financing, or futures contracts trading, a person carrying on the business of dealing in bonds with accredited/expert investors, and the Trustee of a Trust.

questions.q: A Trading Member may allow a customer to trade ONLY AFTER:
o: the account has been opened with the requisite legal documents.
the customer has paid brokerage commissions in advance.
a suitability assessment has been completed.
the risk profile of the customer is established.
questions.e: Only after the account has been opened with the requisite legal documents obtained, suitability assessment completed and risk profile established, then should the customer be allowed to trade within his investment profile.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a Specified Investment Product (SIP) listed on an exchange?
o: Structured warrants.
Equity-linked structured notes.
Credit-linked structured notes.
None of the above.
questions.e: Structured warrants are listed on an exchange. Equity-linked structured notes and credit-linked structured notes are NOT listed.

questions.q: Under which of the following situations a CMS licence holder is NOT required to provide a monthly statement of account to a customer?
o: If there has been no change to the account of the customer in the month.
If the customer is an expert investor to whom such information is already being provided on real-time basis.
If the customer has requested verbally not to receive such information.
All of the above.
questions.e: The Member does not need to send a monthly statement to a customer if the information that is to be contained in the statement has already been sent to the customer by a Clearing House (which the Member is a member of), OR there has been NO change to the customer's account in the month, OR the customer is an Accredited Investor, or a corporation related to the Member (and Real-time electronic statements have been made available to the customer, and the customer has agreed to using these electronic statements, or the customer has requested in WRITING not to receive such monthly statements)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the one-representative-one-principal rule?
o: Ensuring that the principals closely monitor their representatives.
Securing clarity for investors about the status of the representatives.
To ensure that the returns from investments recommended to the clients are maximised.
None of the above.
questions.e: The objectives of the one-representative-one-principal rule are to secure clarity for investors about the status of representatives, the principals they represent, and more importantly, where responsibility rests for complaints and redressal, and to ensure that principals closely monitor and supervise their representatives at all times.

questions.q: Trading Members are required to send monthly statements to customers containing which of the following information?
o: The reason for movement of the assets of the customer.
The movement and balance of money in the customer account.
Net unrealised profits or losses in all open positions of the customer marked to market.
Details of all financial charges and credits to the customer's account even if they have been included in any contract note issued to the customer.
questions.e: Details of all financial charges and credits to the customer's account already included in any contract note issued to the customer NEED NOT included in the monthly statement. The information given in the other options must be included.

questions.q: A provisional representative needs to be previously licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated in relation to a comparable financial advisory service in a comparable overseas jurisdiction for a minimum period of _____.
o: 12 months and not more than 12 months ago.
24 months during his entire career.
24 months and not more than 24 months during the entire career.
12 months during his entire career.
questions.e: A provisional representative needs to be previously licensed, authorised or otherwise regulated in relation to a comparable financial advisory service in a comparable overseas jurisdiction for a minimum period of 12 months (and not more than 12 months ago) in relation to a comparable type of financial advisory service in an overseas jurisdiction, with a regulatory regime that is comparable to that of Singapore.

questions.q: A person may not be considered fit and proper under the Honesty, Integrity and Reputation criteria if he has been a partner in a business which has gone into administration within ____ after the person was the partner in the business.
o: 3 years.
2 years.
1 year.
4 years.
questions.e: A person may not be considered fit and proper under the Honesty, Integrity and Reputation criteria if he has been a partner in a business which has gone into administration within 1 year after the person was the partner in the business.

questions.q: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform ______ of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within ____ after the date of change of the particulars.
o: his principal company; 7 days
his principal company; 14 days
MAS; 7 days
MAS; 14 days
questions.e: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform his principal company of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change of the particulars. The principal company is required to notify MAS of its representative's change of particulars no later than 14 days after the date of the change of the particulars in the prescribed form and manner.

questions.q: John (a provisional representative) changed his residential address on 4 Mar 2024 (Monday) and informed his principal on 8 Mar 2024. John's principal company must inform the MAS by ____ about the change.
questions.e: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform his principal company of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change of the particulars. The principal company is required to notify MAS of its representative's change of particulars no later than 14 days after the date of the change of the particulars in the prescribed form and manner. Therefore, John's principal company must notify MAS within 14 days after 4 Mar 2024, which is 18 Mar 2024.

questions.q: John and Jane work as appointed representatives for LMN Bank. LMN deals in capital market products. John fails to pay a personal loan and receives a court order to pay the lender. Jane is suspended because she has violated LMN's internal code of conduct. LMN discovered that its ex-representative Julie was involved in insider trading. Julie had resigned from LMN to join another CMSL holder 9 months ago. In this context, LMN:
o: Need not file a Report on Misconduct of Representative for Jane because it is a violation of the internal code of conduct leading to suspension, not termination.
Must file a Report on Misconduct of Representative for John to the MAS within 21 days of the date when it discovered that John ceased to be fit and proper.
Must file a Report on Misconduct of Representative for Julie to the MAS within 14 days of the date when it discovered that Julie had committed insider trading.
LMN need not file the Report on Misconduct of Representative for any of the representatives because it is an exempt institution.
questions.e: CMSL holders and exempt institutions must file a "Report on Misconduct of Representative" if any of its representatives fail to meet the "fit and proper" criteria or have committed acts relating to market misconduct within 14 days after the discovery of the misconduct. Misconduct includes a serious breach of the CMS licence holder's or exempt financial institution's internal policy or code of conduct which would render the representative liable to demotion, suspension or termination of the representative's employment. The requirement to report applies to misconduct by ex-representatives also. Please refer to MAS Notice SFA 04-N11.

questions.q: John is 30 years old and sat for GCE O Level Examination in 2013. Which of the following achievements will help him meet the required educational qualifications?
o: 4 GCE O Level credit passes.
2 GCE O Level credit passes with 4 years of relevant and continuous working experience over the past 5 years in respect of the regulated activity.
3 GCE O Level credit passes with 4 years of relevant and continuous working experience over the past 5 years in respect of the regulated activity.
2 GCE O Level credit passes.
questions.e: In the case of a representative who sat for GCE O Level Examinations after 1980, the qualifications should be higher than or equal to at least 4 GCE O Level credit passes.

questions.q: A temporary representative is required to inform about change in his personal particulars to his principal company within ____ of the change in particulars.
o: 3 days.
48 hours.
7 days.
14 days.
questions.e: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform his principal company of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change of the particulars. The principal company is required to notify the MAS of its representative's change of particulars no later than 14 days after the date of the change of the particulars in the prescribed form and manner.

questions.q: In case an appointed representative informs his principal company about change in his residential address, the principal company is ____.
o: Required to notify the MAS within 14 days after receipt of the information from the appointed representative.
Required to notify the MAS within 14 days of the change in particulars.
Required to notify the MAS within 21 days of the change in particulars.
Required to update his records, but is not required to notify the MAS.
questions.e: An appointed, provisional or temporary representative is required to inform his principal company of any change in his residential address or other personal particulars within 7 days after the date of change of the particulars. The principal company is required to notify the MAS of its representative's change of particulars no later than 14 days after the date of the change of the particulars in the prescribed form and manner.

questions.q: Provisional representatives are given a grace period of ____ to complete the requisite examinations as applicable to appointed representatives.
o: 1 month.
3 months.
6 months.
One year.
questions.e: Provisional representatives are given a grace period of 3 months to complete the requisite examinations as applicable to appointed representatives.

questions.q: The status of an appointed representative in respect of any regulated activity ceases if he has stopped to act as a representative for ____, and his principal has not notified the MAS of his cessation as a representative.
o: One year.
Two years.
One month.
6 months.
questions.e: The status of an appointed representative in respect of any regulated activity ceases if he has stopped to act as a representative for one month, and his principal has not notified the MAS of his cessation as a representative.

questions.q: A CMSL holder must inform the MAS within ____ of any change in particulars if it ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licenced for.
o: 7 days
14 days
6 weeks
2 months
questions.e: A CMSL holder must inform the MAS within 14 days of any change in particulars if it ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licenced for.

questions.q: John is the CEO of CMSL holder LMN Corporation. John files for bankruptcy. In this context, which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: MAS has the power of authority to remove John as CEO of LMN.
MAS can only suggest that LMN should remove John as its CEO immediately.
MAS must obtain a court order to remove John as LMN's CEO.
John must step down on his own immediately.
questions.e: MAS has the power of authority to remove the CMS licence holder's executive officers or directors if they fail to meet "fit and proper" criteria, e.g., if they had been convicted of an offence involving fraud and dishonesty, are undischarged bankrupts, failed to discharge their duties of office.

questions.q: In case a CMS licence holder ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licensed for, it is required to inform the MAS of the change in particulars within ____.
o: 1 day.
7 days.
14 days.
30 days.
questions.e: A CMS licence holder is required to inform MAS within 14 days of any change in particulars if it ceases to carry on business in the regulated activity it is licensed for.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Licensee and the custodian responsible for maintaining custody accounts for customers' assets is TRUE?
o: The custodian may claim rights over the customers' assets if the Licensee fails to pay its obligations.
The custodian must provide sufficient information to the Licensee for its compliance to record-keeping obligations under the SFA/SFR.
The custody account must be designated in both the Licensee's and the customer's names.
The custodian may perform internal transfers of customers' assets, as long as the assets remain accounted for.
questions.e: A custodian must provide sufficient info to the holder in order that the holder may comply with its record-keeping obligations under the Act or Regulation or under any other law.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT fall under the definition of Customer's Assets under the SFR?
o: Securities
Government securities
Certificates of deposits
None of the above
questions.e: Customer's assets, in relation to a CMS licence holder, means securities and assets (other than money), including Government securities and certificates of deposits, that are beneficially owned by a customer of the CMS licence holder.

questions.q: May is a trading representative and she received an order from an institutional customer at 10am to buy 3 million shares in ABC Ltd at $5. There was not much supply for ABC Ltd.'s share at $5 but she managed to buy 2 million shares by 4pm that day. Suspecting a good reason for the institutional customer to buy so many of ABC Ltd.'s shares, she traded under her spouse's account to buy 10,000 ABC Ltd shares at $5. She told her husband the reason for the trade. In this scenario, which of the following statements is TRUE?
o: May would be allowed to do that provided she obtained consent from her institutional customer.
May would be allowed to do that provided she obtained approval from MAS.
May was entitled to do what she did.
None of the above.
questions.e: May is not allowed disclose customer info to her husband.

questions.q: Money ____ is NOT considered 'money received on account'.
o: received from the customer for the maintenance of a securities trading account
received for the account of the customer in respect of a sale of securities
which is to be used to reduce the amount owed by the customer to the Licensee
received from the customer where the Licensee provides securities financing to such customer
questions.e: Money received on account of a customer of the CMS licence holder does not include money which is to be used to reduce the amount owed by the customer to the holder.

questions.q: Under the 'Books of holder of capital markets services licence' (SFR (LCB) 39), a Licensee must keep records of:
o: The particulars of the customer's instructions related to the order
The date/time of receipt, amendment or cancellation of the order
The date/time the order, amendment or cancellation is transmitted
The date/time of execution of the order / amended order.
questions.e: SFR (LCB) 39 stipulates that CMS licence holders must keep books and records in English containing details about customer orders.

questions.q: A Licensee may hold customers' moneys on trust for the customers. In which of the following forms of investments can the moneys be held?
o: Government securities.
Any securities or instrument determined by the relevant Authority's guidelines.
Any debt instrument issued by the government of the country of the market/exchange where the Licensee normally transacts in.
Unrated bonds issued by private corporations
